study.format: Restaurant announcement / menu montage: a new-location promo built from build-your-bowl prep and assembly B-roll, cut to a licensed pop song.
study.item: Mediterranean build-your-own bowls from CASSA Kitchen & Catering, plus the hot bar behind them. Bowl components: chopped grilled chicken, crispy dark-brown falafel, tabbouleh, chickpeas, hummus, beets, neon-pink pickled cabbage and turnips, carrots, turmeric-yellow scramble, corn, feta, pita chips and slow-braised shredded beef. What makes it visual is the colour contrast: magenta cabbage against yellow, green herbs and white feta. Creamy tahini and sauce drizzles stripe across the crunchy falafel, and the textures range from crumbly feta to shiny braise.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0–1.6s) is the brick-front 'CASSA Kitchen&Catering' sign shot from a low angle while the camera moves, washed with a big warm orange light leak. The song starts immediately: 'Watermelon sugar high' begins at 0.00s. At 1.6s it hard-cuts on the first beat (audio hit 1.76s) to a macro of glistening charred chicken with 'NEW LOCATION' in large serif caps. The scroll-stopper is the instantly recognisable Harry Styles hook plus a glowing, cinematic-looking sign. Within 2 seconds it shows real food and states the news.

beats.what: Low-angle moving shot of the exterior CASSA sign with an orange light-leak flare; the song's hook line plays.
Macro of chopped grilled chicken in a steel hotel pan; 'NEW LOCATION' text; a rainbow prism flare sweeps across around 2.9s.
Slow move over a finished bowl (beets, white beans, hummus, carrots, chickpeas); 'SAME DELICIOUS FLAVOR'.
Tongs set a falafel into the bowl; 'JOIN US IN ROCKY RIVER / 21619 CENTER RIDGE RD'.
Macro push across crispy falafel with tabbouleh, beets and pistachio-coloured seeds behind; the address text clears around 8.5s.
Tahini starts drizzling across falafel and beets; at 12.2s the squeeze bottle is in frame with a thick stream landing on the falafel.
Hold on falafel striped with tahini, slow push-in.
Spoon lifts a heap of tabbouleh out of the bain-marie; near-still hold.
Bowl with magenta cabbage, turmeric-yellow scramble and red sauce.
White sauce stream pours over the pink cabbage bowl. Around 20s the shot moves to hummus being scooped from the hot bar.
Hot-bar tour: chickpeas with parsley, then tongs in neon-pink cabbage (about 22–24s).
Pink pickled turnips with an orange flare.
Blue object wipe into a spoon in seasoned carrot cubes.
Gloved hands spoon saucy chicken onto rice in a bowl.
More toppings piled onto the chicken: pickled onions, sauce.
Finished falafel bowl covered in shredded cheese and two drizzles; near-still hold around 31.5s.
Colourful bowl in progress: corn, seeds, onions, sauce dome, gloved hands behind.
Hummus scoop dropped into the bowl, followed by a defocus-blur transition around 35.3s.
Spoonful of pita chips tipped onto a feta-and-cabbage bowl, then a near-still hold on the finished bowl (36.5–38s).
Tongs lift a slab of shredded braised beef from the hotel pan; glossy juices.
Salad bowl with sumac onions; feta showered from a spoon at about 43.4s.
Squeeze-bottle sauce zig-zags over feta, corn and cabbage, likely slowed.
Macro of the sauce-laced bowl: pico, feta, potatoes.
Whip and rainbow flare, then a slow pull-back revealing the whole finished bowl (about 50–52.6s).
Interior hanging CASSA sign with 'NOW LOCATED AT 21619 CENTER RIDGE RD ROCKY RIVER 44116' until the end.

study.how_food_is_shown: About 80% of shots are tight macros or close 45° angles, at eye level to slightly above the bowl rim. Food fills the whole 9:16 frame, and the bowl lip often runs along the bottom edge. Almost no wide shots: the only context shots are the two signs, at the start and end. Hands appear in disposable clear gloves (26–35s, 41–44s), along with tongs, spoons, scoops and squeeze bottles. These read as 'made fresh by staff' and show the build-your-bowl service line. Backgrounds are the steel hot bar, bain-maries and sauce bottles, all thrown soft by shallow depth of field. Lighting is warm indoor kitchen light, boosted in the grade, with specular highlights on oily chicken, braise and sauce. Colour is the hero: neon-pink cabbage and turnips against turmeric yellow, parsley green and white feta, all heavily saturated. Texture is pushed by macro distance: crunchy falafel crust, crumbly feta, shreds of beef. The camera is almost always moving with slow gimbal-style pushes, slides or orbits, so even static bowls feel alive.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 1.6–3.97s: macro of charred chicken chunks, about 2.4s with a slow slide. 3.97–6.4s: macro slide over bowl toppings, 2.4s. 8.0–10.2s: falafel crust macro, 2.2s, filling the frame. 10.2–13.0s: tahini drizzle over falafel. Strands are already landing at 11.0s and the bottle stream is in frame at 12.2s; it plays smooth and possibly slightly slowed. 13.0–14.83s: tahini-striped falafel macro held 1.8s. 14.83–16.73s: spoon lifts tabbouleh, near-still around 15–15.5s (motion 15–17). 18.17–~20s: white sauce stream poured over the pink cabbage bowl, about 2s. ~20–21s: hummus scoops in the bain-marie. 21–26.7s: quick 1.2–1.5s ingredient macros of chickpeas, cabbage in tongs, turnips and carrots with a spoon. 36.2–38.77s: pita chips tipped from a spoon, then held nearly still for about 1.5s (motion about 9). 38.77–41.67s: tongs pull up shredded beef with dripping juice, about 2.9s. ~43.4s: feta showered from a spoon, about 1s. 44.03–47.13s: the longest pour, a sauce zig-zag from a squeeze bottle held about 3.1s. It is smooth and slow (motion 14–15 at 45.5–46s), so it is likely real slow motion (medium confidence). 47.13–49.3s: macro of the sauced surface. 49.3–52.67s: orbit, then a slow pull-back to the full bowl. No cheese pulls or cut-opens.
study.money_shot: The tahini drizzle over the crispy falafel, from about 11.0s to 14.83s (about 20–27% of the video). The squeeze-bottle stream hits the falafel at about 12.2s. The pour runs 10.2–13.0s and the striped result is held for another 1.83s (13.0–14.83s). It is set up by 8.0–10.2s of bare, dry falafel macros, so the creamy sauce reads as the payoff. Next comes the tabbouleh spoon-lift. The video echoes this idea later with the 44.03–49.3s sauce zig-zag, which pays off in the full-bowl pull-back reveal at 49.3–52.67s just before the CTA.
study.pacing: Steady, music-driven montage: 25 shots in 55.6s (4.32 cuts per 10s). Shots range 1.17–3.37s, with a median of 2.2s. Ingredient flashes are the fastest: 1.17s at 24.0 and 1.5s at 25.17. Pours and reveals get the longest shots: 2.9s for the tahini pour, 3.1s for the sauce pour, 3.37s for the final bowl reveal and 2.93s for the closing sign. Cuts land on or just before the song's beats. Audio hits at 1.76, 4.19, 6.7, 8.11, 10.62, 26.33, 28.85, 30.73, 32.61, 44.5, 47.67 and 49.58 sit 0.1–0.5s after cuts at 1.6, 3.97, 6.4, 8.0, 10.2, 26.67, 28.6, 30.37, 32.33, 44.03, 47.13 and 49.3. No shot is fully static: median motion is 38.4. Brief near-still holds act as breathers on hero bowls at about 15s, 31.5s, 36.5–38s and 50–55s (motion 9–20). The rhythm is not ASMR; it is a constant, smooth glide.
study.speed: No timelapse and no obvious speed ramps. The pours (10.2–13.0s, 18.17–20s, and especially 44.03–47.13s) move smoothly with low motion (14–15 at 45.5–46s), which suggests mild real slow motion, roughly 50% (medium confidence). Everything else, including gloved assembly, plays at or near real time with smooth camera moves. There is a sharp motion spike of 93.9 at about 49s: a fast whip or flare transition into the final orbit, not a ramp.
study.on_screen_text: All white, all caps, high-contrast serif (Trajan-style) with a soft drop shadow, centred in the middle third, no box. 1.6–3.97s: 'NEW LOCATION' (2 words, one line). 3.97–~6.4s: 'SAME DELICIOUS FLAVOR' (3 words, two lines). 6.4–~8.5s: 'JOIN US IN / ROCKY RIVER' in large type with a smaller line '21619 CENTER RIDGE RD'. Then no text for about 44s while the food carries the video. 52.67–55.6s: 'NOW LOCATED AT / 21619 CENTER RIDGE RD / ROCKY RIVER 44116' in a slightly condensed bold serif, three lines in the lower-middle. No prices, no item names. Each card runs about 2.4s, timed to cut changes.
study.audio: The only audio is Harry Styles' 'Watermelon Sugar', starting on the chorus hook ('Watermelon sugar high' at 0–2s) and continuing through the verse/chorus ('…sounds just like a song' about 34–39s). There is no voiceover, no ASMR kitchen sound and no added SFX. Picture follows the song's pulse: cuts sit on beats, and the brightest moves (flares, the whip at 49s) coincide with audio hits (49.58). The summery, upbeat mood suits the fresh, colourful food.
study.transitions: Mostly hard cuts on the beat. Exceptions: an object wipe at 25.17s, where a blue out-of-focus object sweeps across the lens on both sides of the cut. A defocus blur-through around 35.3s, between the hummus scoop and the pita-chip bowl at 36.2s. A whip-like fast move with a rainbow flare at about 49.3s (motion spike 93.9). Light-leak and prism-flare overlays sit on several cuts (8.0s, 10.2s, 24.0s), softening them. Some content changes inside detected shots (about 20s hummus, about 22s cabbage) suggest extra quick cuts or blur transitions.
study.effects: Heavy warm, saturated grade with lifted contrast and sharpening, so pinks pop neon and browns look caramelised. Orange light-leak overlay on the opening sign (0–1.6s) and at about 24s. Rainbow prism-flare overlays at about 2.9s, 8.0s, 10.2s, 15.6s, 20.3s, 21.4s and 49.2s. Continuous slow push-ins, slides and orbits throughout (gimbal look). Shallow depth of field and an intentional defocus at about 35s. No split screens or freeze frames.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, H.264, about 6 Mbps. It holds up on phone screens, though fine textures are a bit soft and some frames blur during motion (17s, 27s, 49s). Footage is stabilised and gimbal-smooth, with good exposure on the food and dark backgrounds. The high-end feel comes from macro distance, shallow focus, smooth moves and the punchy grade plus flares. The homemade feel comes from the clear plastic gloves, the steel hot-bar setting and the compostable bowls. That mix reads as authentic fast-casual, polished but real.
study.ending: Ends on the CTA. After the final bowl pull-back (49.3–52.67s), it cuts to the interior hanging CASSA sign with the full address text, held for 2.93s with slow camera movement, and cuts at 55.6s mid-song. Opening and closing on the sign bookends the video, so it loops naturally back to the exterior sign at 0s.
study.why_viral: 1) A familiar summer hit with its hook line in the first second makes the post feel upbeat and instantly sticky. 2) Relentless saturated colour: neon-pink pickles, turmeric yellow, green herbs and white feta on almost every shot. 3) Repeated satisfying drizzles over crunchy falafel and loaded bowls, giving a sauce payoff every 10–15 seconds. 4) A clear, short message ('NEW LOCATION / SAME DELICIOUS FLAVOR / address') delivered in the first 8 seconds, then the food sells it, ending on the address.
lessons: Open with a 1–1.6s brand or location shot (sign plus warm light leak), then cut on the first music beat into a full-frame food macro by 2s.
Put the whole message into 3 short text cards (2–5 words each, about 2.4s each) in the first 8s. Then go text-free and let food carry the middle, and bring the address back for the final 3s.
Use one strong typeface: white all-caps serif with a soft shadow, centred in the middle third, at most 3 lines.
Keep a median shot of about 2.2s. Flash ingredients at 1.2–1.5s, but give drizzles and reveals 2.9–3.4s.
Cut each shot 0.1–0.5s ahead of a music beat so the change feels locked to the song.
Show the bare item first (crispy falafel, about 2s), then the sauce drizzle over it, then hold the sauced result for about 1.8s. The before/after makes the pour the payoff.
Repeat a pour or drizzle every 10–15s across a 55s montage. Shoot pours at 50–60fps and slow them down to roughly half speed.
Keep the camera moving slowly (push, slide, orbit) on every food shot. Use 1–2s near-still holds only on finished hero bowls.
Grade warm and saturated, and frame for colour contrast: put the brightest ingredient (pink pickles, yellow corn) against white or green in every shot.
Use light-leak or prism flares and object wipes sparingly, on 4–7 cuts, to make phone footage feel cinematic without hiding the food.

study.format: Product showcase / menu reveal: a dessert-case lookbook for a coffee shop (Shibam Coffee, Cleveland). Single-item hero shots set to a music track, then wide 'full spread' shots and a closing brand sign. No process, no bite, no voiceover.
study.item: About 12 plated desserts on white branded rectangular plates and one bamboo board. They include a caramel-glazed tres leches with a white chevron drizzle; trompe-l'oeil fruit-shaped mousse desserts (glossy pink raspberry, matte navy blueberry, seed-dotted red strawberry, yellow pineapple with green leaves); a layered cake cup topped with red/white/blue nonpareils; a pistachio tres leches with green drizzle and nuts; a Biscoff cheesecake; an Oreo/cocoa cream cake; a Ferrero-topped tres leches sitting in a puddle of milk; a chocolate-peanut brownie with a green zigzag; and tiramisu. The visual draw is strong color variety against white, the clean cut layers, and the realistic fake fruits.
study.hook: Frame 0 opens tight at about 45° on the caramel tres leches square: a glossy amber top, crisp white chevron piping and a visible sponge/cream cross-section on a white plate, with a slow drift. Music starts at once with beat hits at 0.28, 0.54 and 0.76s, and the lyric 'Mojo deal with' runs 0.43–1.37s. It stops the scroll because the graphic chevron pattern and the clean layered cut read instantly as 'premium bakery dessert' with zero text needed. The quick fruit-shaped desserts that follow (2.03–3.07s) add a 'wait, is that real fruit?' double-take.

beats.what: Caramel chevron tres leches, slow drift at 45°, held 2.03s.
Pink raspberry-shaped mousse on a 'Shibam Coffee Co.' plate, 0.43s, cut near beat 2.07.
Navy blueberry-shaped mousse, 0.6s.
Strawberry-shaped mousse with seed texture, nearly still hold (motion 0.8) to about 4.0s, cut on beat 3.1.
Layered cake cup with red/white/blue nonpareils, reached via a fast motion-blur move (motion 39.7), held to 5.2s.
Pistachio tres leches, 0.63s, exiting on a blur whip that passes through near-black at about 5.8s.
Biscoff cheesecake on a bamboo board, static hold of about 1.7s.
Oreo/cocoa cream cake, entered with a whip (motion about 40), held about 1.5s.
Ferrero tres leches in a milk puddle, entered via whip (motion 57.3), held about 1.5s.
Chocolate-peanut brownie with a green zigzag.
Pineapple-shaped mousse, then a quick move to tiramisu at about 12.4s.
Wide reveal of the full spread of plates on the counter under gold 'COFFEE' letters.
Low eye-level shot: strawberry, nonpareil cup and blurred brownie in the foreground, gold COFFEE sign behind.
High-angle wide of the entire dessert lineup, all items at once, cut near audio hit 14.15.
Low glide past the chevron tres leches with the gold letters bokeh'd behind.
Dutch-angle pass over the pistachio tres leches toward the gold letters.
Push-in on the chevron tres leches again, a callback to the hook item, 1.47s.
Tilted slow move over the mirrored gold 'Shibam COFFEE' wall sign as a brand sign-off, 1.63s to the end.

study.how_food_is_shown: Single items are shot at about 30–45° from slightly above, mid-close, one dessert centered per frame. The backgrounds are a seamless off-white tabletop and wall, so each dessert's color pops. The white plates carry the printed Shibam logo as passive branding. Depth of field is shallow, with backgrounds falling to soft cream. There are no hands in frame. Lighting is soft, diffused and warm-neutral (window or softbox): even exposure, gentle shadows, speculars on glazes (the caramel top, the raspberry gloss). The second half switches to environment shots: a low counter-level angle with foreground desserts out of focus, high-angle wides of the whole spread, and dutch tilts that work the gold acrylic 'COFFEE' and 'Shibam' signage into the frame. The emphasis is cross-section layers (sponge/cream/glaze), surface texture (nonpareils, strawberry seeds, cocoa dust) and color contrast.
study.close_ups_and_pours:
There are no pours, drips, cheese pulls or cut-opens; it is pure plated-product close-ups.
- 0–2.03s: caramel chevron cake, the tightest framing, with a slight drift.
- 2.03–2.47s: raspberry mousse (0.43s).
- 2.47–3.07s: blueberry mousse (0.6s).
- About 3.07–4.0s: strawberry mousse, frozen-still close-up showing its seed texture.
- About 4.2–5.2s: nonpareil cup, sprinkles in focus, cup layers soft.
- 5.2–5.83s: pistachio tres leches (nuts and green drizzle).
- About 5.83–7.6s: Biscoff cheesecake, embossed cookie logo visible.
- About 8.0–9.5s: Oreo cake with cocoa dust and a half Oreo.
- About 9.9–11.3s: Ferrero tres leches, the milk soak pooling on the plate (the closest thing to a 'wet' shot).
- About 11.6–12.0s: brownie zigzag.
- About 12.0–12.3s: pineapple mousse.
- About 12.4–13.0s: tiramisu.
All play at normal speed with near-zero camera motion (motion 0.4–1.3) during holds.
study.money_shot: The full-spread reveal at 14.2–15.13s (about 71% into the video, held 0.93s). A high-angle wide shows every dessert introduced so far, laid out together under the gold 'COFFEE' letters. It is set up by 13s of one-at-a-time close-ups, so the viewer recognises each item, and by a low teaser angle at 13.3s with the strawberry and cup in front of the sign. It is followed by low glides back into individual cakes and the brand sign. The single most appetizing frame is the 0–2s chevron tres leches close-up, the item they return to at 17.0s.
study.pacing: Fast and fairly even: 13 detected shots plus about 6 internal whip transitions the cut detector missed, so roughly 19 distinct views in 20.1s. Cut rate is 5.97 cuts per 10s, with a median shot of 1.23s. The opening runs 2.03s, then a burst of 0.43s and 0.6s fruit shots on the beat. The middle has hidden 1.3–1.7s still holds per dessert, joined by blur whips at about 4.2, 7.8, 9.7 and 11.5s. The ambience section from 13.3s uses 0.63–1.63s moving shots. The music hits roughly every 0.26s from 0–5.15s. Cuts at 2.03, 3.07 and 5.2 land within 0.05s of hits 2.07, 3.1 and 5.15, and 14.2 sits near 14.15. Median motion is a low 8.6: calm holds punctuated by sharp spikes.
study.speed: No real slow motion: there are no liquids or falling elements, and holds are just steady near-static frames with motion 0.4–1.3. There are no timelapses. Motion spikes of 37–57 at about 4.0, 5.5–6.0, 7.5–8.0, 9.5 and 11.5–12.5s are fast camera whips/swipes with heavy motion blur used as transitions, not speed ramps (moderate confidence). The ambience shots from 13.3s are smooth gimbal-style glides at normal speed.
study.on_screen_text: none
study.audio: A music track only; there is no voiceover and no ASMR. The three detected words 'Mojo deal with' (0.43–1.37s) are song lyrics. Dense rhythmic hits every about 0.26s from 0.28 to 5.15s drive the quick fruit-dessert cuts, which are synced at 2.03, 3.07 and 5.2s. The hits thin out mid-video, then return at 13.71, 14.15, 15.96, 16.86, 17.76, 19.55 and 20.04 as the spread and sign shots play. There are no food sounds; mood comes entirely from the track.
study.transitions: Hard cuts on the beat at 2.03, 2.47 and 3.07s. There are whip/swipe transitions with strong directional motion blur at about 4.2s (strawberry→cup), 5.2–5.83s (the pistachio cake smears sideways at 5.18, then the camera passes through a near-black frame at 5.79 before the Biscoff), about 7.8s, about 9.7s, about 11.5s and about 12.4s. The rest, at 13.3, 14.2, 15.13, 15.77, 17.0 and 18.47s, are hard cuts between moving shots.
study.effects: A warm, slightly lifted grade: creamy whites, boosted saturation on the reds, blues and greens, and gold signage glowing. Shallow-depth-of-field bokeh is used heavily in the ambience shots. There is mild softness/smoothing consistent with upscaling or compression. Dutch tilts appear at 15.77s and 18.47s. Push-ins come from camera moves, e.g. 17.0s, not digital zoom. There are no freeze frames, split screens, light leaks or overlays.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264, about 5.5 Mbps: decent but soft, with fine detail (cake crumb, sprinkles) slightly smeared, likely recompressed or upscaled. Shots are very stable (tripod/gimbal) with clean, even exposure, no blown highlights and low noise. It looks high-end because of the styling rather than resolution: a minimal white-on-cream palette, branded plates, one hero item per frame, shallow focus and the gold acrylic signage. The softness is the main homemade tell.
study.ending: Ends on the tilted, slowly moving shot of the mirrored gold 'Shibam COFFEE' sign (18.47–20.1s, 1.63s), with a fruit-shaped dessert peeking at the bottom. It is a brand sign-off rather than food, landing about 1.6s after the last food shot. It cuts on an audio hit at 20.04s. It doesn't loop perfectly, but returning to the chevron cake at 0s makes a replay feel continuous with the 17.0s callback.
study.why_viral: 1) Novelty: hyper-real fruit-shaped mousse desserts (raspberry, blueberry, strawberry, pineapple) trigger 'is that real?' curiosity and rewatches. 2) Variety plus color: about 12 visually distinct desserts in 20s, each a different color story against white, flashed on the beat so nobody gets bored. 3) Cross-section porn: clean tres leches and cake layers, glossy glazes and milk puddles signal moist and indulgent. 4) The spread-reveal payoff plus luxe gold branding makes it feel like a destination café worth visiting.
lessons: Open on your most graphic, best-cut item at a 30–45° angle and hold it about 2s; a strong pattern or clean layer cross-section beats any text hook.
Show one dessert per frame on a plain light background and branded plates, so color contrast does the work and the logo appears without overlays.
Burst your most surprising items in 0.4–0.6s shots right after the hook, cutting within ±0.05s of music hits.
For a menu run, hold each item 1.3–1.7s nearly still (motion under 2) and link items with fast whip-blur transitions instead of plain cuts to keep energy high.
After 10–13s of individual items, pay off with a wide 'everything together' spread shot at about 65–75% of runtime.
Use low counter-level angles with foreground desserts in soft focus and signage behind to sell the venue, not just the food.
Bring the hook item back near the end (here at 17.0s) to create a loop feel and reinforce the hero product.
End on 1.5–2s of brand signage with a slow tilted move instead of a text CTA; it works as the call to action for local cafés.
Keep the total around 20s with a median shot of about 1.2s, about 6 cuts per 10s.

study.format: product showcase / drink reveal (empty-cup-to-finished-drinks swap transition)
study.item: Two iced café drinks in branded clear can-shaped glasses from Shibam Coffee Co.: an Iced Cookie Butter Latte (caramel-orange base with white milk swirls, cold-foam cap, crushed cookie crumble on top) and a Strawberry Matcha (bright pink strawberry milk bottom, vivid green matcha middle layer, white foam, freeze-dried strawberry dust on top). The visual pull is the stark color layering (orange/white vs pink/green/white) seen through clear glass.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0.0s): two empty, upside-down branded can glasses on a white marble counter, gloved barista hands framing them, Shibam apron logo in view. The first word lands at 0.00s, a sassy voice saying 'Like, girl, I'm gonna slaughter this', over a beat with hits every ~0.24s. The empty cups plus the confident boast set up a 'what's going in these?' promise. At ~0.5s the hands lift the glasses up out of frame, creating instant motion (motion 43.4 at 1.0s).

beats.what: Empty upside-down glasses on marble, gloved hands, voice line 'Like, girl, I'm gonna slaughter this' starts immediately
Hands grab and lift both glasses up and out of frame, leaving apron and counter
Huge translucent drink-name text ('STRAWBERRY… MATCHA') slides across the empty apron frame, previewing the reveal
Hard cut: the glasses come back down, now full of finished drinks, with giant zoomed-in title text over them
Text shrinks to small labels 'ICED COOKIE BUTTER LATTE' / 'STRAWBERRY MATCHA' above each drink; hands set them down
Hands slide away; drinks held as a static hero shot with a slow camera drift showing the layers and toppings
Slight camera move/text shift as the clip ends on the two finished drinks

study.how_food_is_shown: Locked-off eye-level frontal shot at counter height, drinks centered in the lower-middle third on white veined marble that bounces soft light into the glass. Barista's torso in black denim apron with the brand logo fills the background (a branding prop), and black nitrile gloves give a clean, professional look and contrast against the pastel drinks. Soft, warm-neutral diffused light with no harsh shadows, shallow depth of field so the apron goes soft behind the sharp cups. Color emphasis is on the layer bands visible through clear glass and the crumb/strawberry toppings at the rim.
study.close_ups_and_pours: No pours, drips or macro shots. The closest framing is the hero shot of both drinks at about 1/3 frame height, held from ~1.7s to 5.4s (~3.7s) at normal speed with a slight drift/push-in that lets the topping texture (cookie crumble, strawberry dust) and the streaky milk swirls read.
study.money_shot: The full drinks side by side with name labels, landing right after the cut at 1.4s (26% in) and settling by ~2.5s (46%) once the hands move away. It is held ~3-4s until the end. It's set up by the empty-glass hook and the lift-out-of-frame move, so the 'empty → full' swap pays off instantly. Nothing follows it. The video ends on it.
study.pacing: Just 2 shots: 1.4s of hook/setup, then a 4.0s hold (1.85 cuts per 10s). The opening is fast and kinetic, with motion peaking at 43.4 around 1.0s as the cups are lifted and text flies in. The rest is calm, with motion around 4-10 as the hero hold settles. The single cut at 1.4s sits right on an audio hit (1.36s), and the music pulses every ~0.24s. Overall it's a quick 5.4s loop-length piece.
study.speed: None clearly visible. Everything appears to play at normal speed. The motion blur at 0.84-1.18s comes from the fast lift and animated text, not a ramp (moderate confidence).
study.on_screen_text: Two text treatments. (1) Transition text from ~1.0s to ~1.6s: giant white heavy condensed all-caps letters with a dark drop shadow, semi-transparent at first, sweeping across and oversized/cropped ('STRAWBE… / …TERMATCH'), then scaling down. (2) Labels from ~1.7s to the end: white bold condensed all-caps with a subtle shadow, two lines each, placed directly above each drink ('ICED COOKIE / BUTTER LATTE' left, 'STRAWBERRY / MATCHA' right), 2-3 words per label. No prices.
study.audio: An opening trending sound/voice clip says 'Like, girl, I'm gonna slaughter this' (0.00-1.30s). It runs over a steady beat with hits every ~0.24s (0.15, 0.36 … 5.25). There are no ASMR sounds such as ice or pours. The cut and reveal at 1.4s line up with a beat hit at 1.36s, right as the line finishes.
study.transitions: One hard cut at 1.4s, disguised as a magic swap. The hands lift the empty cups out of frame, the scene shows only the apron with giant text sweeping over it, and the cut lands as the full drinks drop back into the same position. Because the framing matches on both sides, it reads as a match cut / object-reveal swap, with the big text acting as a wipe that covers the edit.
study.effects: Animated kinetic title text that scales from huge/cropped to small labels. There is slight motion blur during the transition and a subtle slow drift/push-in on the hero shot. The grade is mildly warm with soft contrast and clean whites, and the pinks and greens are saturated without looking neon.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, 3.5 Mbps h264. Acceptable but softened by recompression: the labels and logo are a bit mushy, with some ghosting. The tripod-locked camera, clean marble, uniform gloves and branded glassware make it look professional and café-produced rather than homemade, even at modest resolution.
study.ending: Ends on the static hero shot of both finished drinks with labels, ~3s after the reveal settles. There is no CTA or sip. The short 5.4s length and the static end frame encourage rewatching, but it doesn't loop seamlessly back to the empty cups.
study.why_viral: 1) The empty-to-full swap is a magic-trick payoff delivered in under 1.5s, short enough that people rewatch to catch it. 2) Striking, contrasting layered colors (caramel vs pink/green) in clear glass look great and photograph instantly. 3) A sassy trending voice line gives personality and sets up an expectation the reveal pays off. 4) Clear name labels make the drinks instantly orderable and shareable ('get me the strawberry matcha').
lessons: Start on the 'before' state (empty cups, raw ingredients) for ~1-1.5s, then hard-cut to the finished item in the same framing for a magic-swap reveal.
Hide the swap cut behind motion: have hands lift the object out of frame, and/or sweep oversized text across the frame, and cut on that cover.
Land the reveal cut on a music beat; here the cut at 1.4s sits on a hit at 1.36s.
Lock the camera on a tripod at eye/counter level so the before and after frames line up exactly.
Show drinks in clear glassware against a bright, neutral surface (white marble) so the color layers carry the shot.
After the reveal, hold the hero shot still for 3-4s with only a gentle drift so viewers can read layers and toppings.
Label each item with 2-3 word bold white all-caps names placed directly above it so viewers know what to order.
Keep it under ~6s with only 2 shots for showcase reveals; brevity drives rewatches.
Put branding in the set (apron logo, printed cups) instead of overlaying logos, and use matching gloves/uniform for a pro look.

study.format: Making-of / process montage turned event promo: a vendor's (Fire & Dough) knafa built from tray to plate, cut as an ad for 'NEO Suhoor Fest, Feb 20 & 21'.
study.item: Authentic Palestinian knafa (kunafa). Neon-yellow semolina/kataifi crumb is pressed into a copper tray and covered with crumbly white cheese. It is baked to a deep burnt-orange crust, flooded with glossy clear syrup, then lifted on a spatula to show long stretchy white cheese strings. It is served on a fluted gold paper plate under bright green crushed pistachio. The visual draw is the strong colour story: yellow, then white, then orange, then gold and green, plus the stretchy cheese.
study.hook: First frame (0-0.73s): a black-gloved hand smears a pat of butter or ghee across a huge shiny copper tray. A warm orange light streak runs across the frame. A yellow highlight box is already wiping on as the title types out word by word ('AUTHENT…' by 0.73s, 'AUTHENTIC' at 0.92s, 'PALESTINIAN' by 1.54s, 'KNAFA' complete about 2.77s). The only voice line, 'That's it.', lands at 0.46-1.24s over music. It stops the scroll because the copper tray is huge and shiny, and the animated yellow title names a specific, heritage-coded dish within 3s.

beats.what: Gloved hand buttering the copper tray; yellow title box begins typing 'AUTHENTIC'; voice 'That's it.' at 0.46s.
Close shot of the hand smearing butter in circles; 'PALESTINIAN' types in.
Wide swirl of greased tray with kitchen behind; bright yellow crumb rains into the tray at about 2.0s; 'KNAFA' completes.
Macro of a gloved hand pressing the neon-yellow crumb base.
Low 45° angle across the tray rim as a palm flattens the yellow layer; lower-third 'FIRE & DOUGH / NEO SUHOOR FEST' slides in at about 4.5s.
Handful of white cheese dropped onto the yellow base, close-up.

Cheese spread across the tray, eye-level with a shallow-focus background. Around 9.5s (motion spike to 72.9) it shifts to a low macro glide over cheese dusted with more crumb and green pistachio, until 12.3s.
Baked knafa revealed on the burner as the copper lid lifts: deep orange crust with a rainbow lens flare across it.
Second angle of the crust under the lifting lid; a cloth-held lid comes off by 13.8s.
Ladle of clear syrup poured onto the orange crust, low eye-level macro.
Low macro glide across the syrup-soaked, glistening crust.
Knife slices into the crust (0.47s shot).
Spatula slides under a square and slowly lifts it; long white cheese strings stretch from the gooey yellow interior. Rainbow flares pass over it. Held 6.07s.
Plated portion on a gold fluted paper plate, piled with pistachio, with syrup still drizzling from above.
Plastic fork digs into the plate through a warm orange light-leak flash.
Fork lifts a bite with a long cheese pull while the 'NEO Suhoor Fest / Feb 20 & 21' card holds to the end at 29.5s.

study.how_food_is_shown: Almost everything is shot close and low, at eye level or about 15-45° just above the tray rim. The rim works as a leading line, and the food fills 70-90% of the vertical frame. Hands are in black nitrile gloves, which make the yellow crumb and white cheese pop and read as a professional kitchen. A plain hand holds the knife and spatula later. Backgrounds are steel kitchen counters, a grey concrete wall and a blurry blue venue. All are thrown out of focus with shallow depth of field so only the food is sharp. Lighting is bright, even and warm, with strong specular highlights on the copper, syrup and crust. Added rainbow/prism flares and orange light leaks give a golden-hour look. The colour sequence is deliberate: neon yellow (3-7s), then white on yellow (7-12s), then burnt orange (12-23s), then gold plate with green pistachio (23-29.5s). Each phase looks different, and the texture contrast runs crumb, crumble, crust, gloss, stretch.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0-1.53s: macro of butter smeared on copper, real speed. About 2.0-3.2s: yellow crumb cascades into the tray, medium-close, real speed. 3.2-4.27s: macro of the pressed crumb texture, frame filled edge to edge. 4.27-6.8s: low macro across the rim of the yellow layer with a hand pressing. 6.8-7.73s: close-up of the cheese drop. 7.73-12.3s: cheese spread, then an extreme low macro skim over the cheese/crumb/pistachio surface, held about 2.8s. 12.3-13.93s: lid lift off the orange crust, close. 13.93-15.0s: syrup ladle pour, held 1.07s, very close and low so the liquid sheet catches light. 15.0-16.6s: macro glide over the glossy syrup surface, 1.6s. 16.6-17.07s: knife cut, 0.47s. 17.07-23.13s: spatula lift and cheese pull. This is the longest hold (6.07s) and close enough that the slice fills about half the frame. Motion reads 6-11, so it is almost certainly slow-motion (high confidence). 23.13-24.97s: thin syrup stream drizzling onto the plated knafa, 1.83s. 25.87-29.5s: fork cheese pull from the plate, 3.63s, also low motion (7.8-12.1), likely mild slow motion.
study.money_shot: The spatula cheese pull at 17.07-23.13s (58%-78% of the video), held 6.07s in slow motion. It is set up by a quick escalation: lid reveal (0.53s), syrup pour (1.07s), glossy macro (1.6s) and a 0.47s knife cut that snaps straight into the lift. The music hits start at 17.08s, exactly on the cut into it. Rainbow flares drift across as the strings stretch. It is followed by the plated reveal at 23.13s and a second, smaller cheese pull on the fork (25.87-29.5s) under the event CTA, so the video ends on the same payoff.
study.pacing: Mixed. The opener is fast: the first four shots are 0.73, 0.8, 1.67 and 1.07s while the title types. Prep then slows (2.53s, 0.93s, 4.57s) to let textures read. A rapid build follows from 12.3-17.07s (0.53, 1.1, 1.07, 1.6, 0.47s) into one long 6.07s hold. The ending is 1.83s, 0.9s and a 3.63s final hold. Overall: 16 shots in 29.5s, 5.08 cuts/10s, median shot 1.08s. The longest shots (4.57s, 6.07s) are reserved for texture and the cheese pull. From 17s on the music hits arrive about every 0.25-0.6s. The cuts at 17.07 and 24.97 sit on hits (17.08, 24.95), and the cut at 25.87 lands just before the 26.06 hit.
study.speed: Slow motion on the spatula cheese pull at 17.07-23.13s: motion drops to 6-11 while strings stretch smoothly (high confidence). Probable mild slow motion on the final fork pull at 26.5-29s (motion 7.8-12) and on the syrup pour/glide at 15-16.5s (9-17) (medium confidence). Prep shots at 0-12s look like normal speed; the higher motion there (up to 46.8) comes from hand action and camera glides. The 72.9 spike at 9.5s is an internal transition or fast move within the 7.73-12.3 shot, not a timelapse. No timelapses.
study.on_screen_text: 1) Title stack 'AUTHENTIC / PALESTINIAN / KNAFA': heavy condensed sans, black, all caps, each word on its own yellow box with darker yellow hatched borders. It is centred in the upper third (about y 20-40%). A glowing yellow highlight bar wipes in first, then letters type on, one word at a time: AUTHENTIC 0.3-0.9s, PALESTINIAN by about 1.5s, KNAFA about 2.1-2.8s. It holds to 4.27s, at most 3 words. 2) Lower-third at about 4.5-6.8s, bottom-left: 'FIRE & DOUGH / NEO SUHOOR FEST', black condensed bold caps on white bars with an orange vertical accent stripe, sliding in from the left. 3) CTA card at about 25.5-29.5s: 'NEO Suhoor Fest / Feb 20 & 21' in the same white-bar/orange-stripe style, title case, upper-left/centre, sliding in from the left and holding to the end. No prices.
study.captions: none (only two words are spoken, at 0.46-1.24s, and they are not captioned)
study.audio: Licensed music runs throughout. The Instagram audio tag shows Maher Zain – 'Free Palestine', a nasheed-style track that reinforces the Palestinian framing. A single voice line, 'That's it.', comes at 0.46s. The strongest audio hits cluster from 17.08s onward (17.08, 18.68, 19.91, then every 0.25-0.5s through 28.88), so the music swells right as the cheese pull starts and carries the ending. No clearly isolated ASMR sizzle or crunch; the food is sold visually.
study.transitions: Mostly hard cuts, dressed with effects. 1.53s: hard cut with an orange light-leak flash. 3.2s: the outgoing frame is soft and blurry, a short blur/zoom into the macro. 4.27s: zoom/whip blur with an orange-pink leak (the before-frame is motion-blurred). About 9.5s: a hidden transition inside the 7.73-12.3 shot (motion spike 72.9), likely a quick blur or dissolve into the topped-cheese macro. 12.3, 12.83 and 13.93s: hard cuts. 15.0, 16.6 and 17.07s: hard cuts, the last on the beat. 24.97s: warm light-leak flash/blur into the fork dig. 25.87s: hard cut.
study.effects: Heavy warm grade with high saturation (neon yellows, deep oranges) and boosted contrast. Strong sharpening on textures. Rainbow prism flares are overlaid repeatedly: 12.3-14s on the lid reveal, 16.9s, 18.1-18.7s, 22.4-23s on the cheese pull, and 26.7-29s on the final pull. Orange/pink light leaks appear at about 0.3s, 1.5s, 4.0s and 24.9s. Glow and typewriter animation on the title boxes, and slide-ins on the lower-thirds. Mild push-ins and glides on macros (7.73-12.3s, 15-16.6s). No split screens or freeze frames.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264 at about 5.9 Mbps: fine for phones but not crisp 1080. Footage looks phone-shot and handheld, with smooth gimbal-like glides on the macros. Some shots show compression softness and upscale blur (2-4s, 9.5-12s). Exposure is bright and clean with no crushed shadows. The high-end feel comes less from resolution than from: shallow-focus macros, black gloves and copper/steel trays, saturated warm grading, shiny syrup highlights and the gold plate. Together these make a festival food stall look premium.
study.ending: Ends on the CTA plus a second money shot: a slow fork cheese pull over the gold plate, with 'NEO Suhoor Fest / Feb 20 & 21' held about 4s (25.5-29.5s). It cuts mid-stretch with no outro. The rising cheese pull and dangling strings make it loop loosely back to the buttery copper tray.
study.why_viral: 1) A 6s slow-motion cheese pull out of syrup-glazed orange crust, the most craveable texture there is, landing right where the music kicks in. 2) A bold colour progression (neon yellow, white, orange, gold and green) makes every phase look new and keeps viewers watching the transformation. 3) An identity- and season-loaded hook ('AUTHENTIC PALESTINIAN KNAFA', Suhoor/Ramadan, Maher Zain track) gives the community a reason to share and tag. 4) Satisfying process steps (crumb rain, pressing, cheese drop, syrup pour, knife cut) build anticipation before the payoff, and the ad ends on a second pull plus a concrete date.
lessons: Put the dish name in the first 3s as a typed-on, word-by-word title in high-contrast boxes (here 3 words, 0.3-2.8s), and remove it by about 4s so the food takes over.
Save one 5-7s slow-motion hold for the single best texture moment (cheese pull, drip, cut-open) around 55-75% of the runtime. Keep everything else around 0.5-1.7s.
Build into the money shot with a fast run of 4-5 short shots (0.5-1.6s each: reveal, pour, glossy macro, cut) and land the cut into it on a music hit.
Shoot prep from low, near-rim angles (15-45°) with macro distance so the food fills 70%+ of the frame, and blur the kitchen with shallow focus.
Sequence shots by colour and texture change (raw, layered, baked, glazed, plated) so each segment looks visually different, and push saturation and warmth on golden or orange foods.
Use black gloves or dark props against bright ingredients for contrast and a professional look. Glossy liquids (syrup, butter) need a hard key light to catch highlights.
End on a second, smaller payoff (a fork pull or bite) with the CTA (event name and date, or location and price) held at least 3-4s, rather than a static end card.
Use light leaks and flares sparingly as transitions (here 3-4 orange flashes) and on the hero shot. Do not cover the food texture itself.
Match the music to the story and audience, and start the strongest beats right on the money shot. Here the hits begin at 17.08s, on the 17.07s cut.

study.format: Making-of / process (restaurant griddle cook, ASMR-style macro b-roll set to a licensed song, no voiceover)
study.item: Shell-on jumbo shrimp seared on a flat-top griddle in bubbling butter, dusted with red seasoning, streamed with a golden sauce and tossed until glossy and lacquered red-orange. The visual appeal comes from the colour change from translucent pink-white to deep paprika red, the constant foaming butter bubbles, glossy sauce sheen and the crusty seasoning texture on the shells.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0.0s) is an extreme macro, lens almost at griddle level, of a pile of pink-and-white shell-on shrimp sitting in foaming golden butter. Tiny bubbles pop around the shells and the background falls off into blur. There is no text. The audio opens on a hit at 0.05s and the song's first lyric, "So", lands at 0.94s. It stops the scroll because the shrimp fill the whole vertical frame with texture and movement (the sizzle bubbles) before you've worked out what you're looking at. Raw-looking shrimp also creates a 'what will this become' tension.

beats.what: Macro of shell-on shrimp sizzling in bubbling butter on the griddle
Seasoning dust rains down from above onto the shrimp; particles float through the frame and the shells turn orange
Thin golden stream of sauce/butter poured over the paprika-coated shrimp, with droplets catching the light
Spatula slides in and presses/tosses the shrimp; sauce foams red-orange on the griddle
Shrimp now glazed glossy red, tossed between two spatulas
Spatula edge scrapes and flips the saucy shrimp, with bubbling sauce and dark griddle surface visible
Low shot of the glazed shrimp sizzling, with the house sauce bottle (red cap) blurred behind as a brand prop
Spatula lifts away in the background while the shrimp bubble in the foreground
Tight macro of one lacquered shrimp coated in seasoning crust, very shallow focus, dark background
4.27s held macro of the finished paprika-crusted shrimp on the griddle with butter bubbling around them, slow camera drift

study.how_food_is_shown: Almost every shot is a macro at griddle level (0–15° above the surface), with the lens a few centimetres from the shrimp. That makes each shrimp look huge and makes the griddle surface a textured foreground. Depth of field is very shallow: the hero shrimp is sharp while the back of the griddle, the steel hood and the sauce bottle melt into blur, which isolates colour and texture. Hands never appear; only the tools (two metal spatulas, a squeeze-bottle stream, seasoning falling from above) enter the frame. The light is warm and directional, with specular highlights on the glossy sauce and the butter bubbles. The background is neutral grey/black steel, so the orange-red food pops. The colour arc is the story: pale pink/white with yellow butter (0–1.8s), then dusted orange (1.8–4.8s), then saturated glossy red (4.8s onward), then a deep red crust with darker char (9.93s onward).
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0–1.8s: extreme macro of shrimp in foaming butter, held 1.8s, bubbles moving. 1.8–3.27s: macro of seasoning particles falling through the air and settling on the shells, 1.47s; the floating dust and low motion (2.0–3.7) suggest slow motion, moderate confidence. 3.27–4.8s: the pour, a thin golden stream into the frame top-left hitting the shrimp, with stray droplets suspended in the air at ~4.5s. Held 1.53s, very close, smooth stream, likely slowed slightly (moderate confidence). 4.8–5.73s: spatula push/toss, sauce foaming, 0.93s, the highest-motion moment (21.8). 5.73–7.07s: glossy glaze close-up while tossing. 7.07–8.0s: spatula edge scraping under the shrimp. 8.0–8.9s and 8.9–9.93s: sizzling glazed shrimp with tools in the background. 9.93–11.53s: 1.6s macro of a single crusted shrimp showing seasoning granules and sauce gloss. 11.53–15.8s: 4.27s macro hold of the finished shrimp with butter bubbles popping. There's no cheese pull, no cut-open and no bite.
study.money_shot: The final hold from 11.53s to 15.8s (starts at ~73% of the video, held 4.27s, the longest shot by far): a macro of the paprika-crusted, glossy red shrimp piled on the griddle, butter still bubbling around them, with the camera drifting gently. It's set up by the 9.93s single-shrimp macro, which slows the rhythm, and by the colour transformation that runs through the earlier shots, so the viewer arrives at the finished, saturated version. Nothing follows it; the video ends on this shot.
study.pacing: Fast cuts for the process, then one long hold for the payoff. Shots 1–9 run 0.9–1.8s each (median 1.4s, 5.7 cuts per 10s), and the middle tossing section (4.8–9.93s) is the fastest at 0.9–1.33s per shot. The final shot is 4.27s, more than twice any other. The first three cuts land on audio hits (1.8 vs hit 1.75, 3.27 vs 3.26, 4.8 vs 4.75), and 5.73 is close to 5.83. Later cuts (7.07, 8.0, 8.9, 9.93, 11.53) sit between hits, so the edit follows the song loosely after 6s. Motion is moderate throughout (median 10.1) and settles to ~7–8 in the final hold, giving a calm ASMR finish.
study.speed: Likely mild slow motion on the seasoning dust (1.8–3.27s), where motion drops to 2.0–3.7 while particles visibly float. Also likely on the sauce pour (3.27–4.8s), where the stream is smooth and droplets hang mid-air. Confidence is moderate. The final hold (11.53–15.8s) may also be gently slowed, given the soft bubble movement and low motion (~7–8). There are no obvious speed ramps or timelapses. The spike to 32.3 at 15.5s is the clip ending or looping, not a ramp.
study.on_screen_text: none
study.audio: A licensed song (Olivia Dean, "So Easy (To Fall In Love)") plays throughout; its first lyric "So" lands at 0.94s. There is no voiceover. Audio hits fall at a steady ~0.43s spacing from 9.26s onward (9.26, 9.68, 10.11, 10.54, 10.97, 11.39), following the song's rhythm. Early cuts are placed on hits (1.75/1.8, 3.26/3.27, 4.75/4.8). The sizzle isn't clearly separated from the music, so the video leans on visual sizzle (bubbles) rather than ASMR sound. The warm, romantic track frames the food as an easy-to-love comfort dish.
study.transitions: Hard cuts only. Several are near-match cuts on the same subject and angle: 1.8 (same shrimp pile, now dusted), 3.27 (same pile, now a pour), 5.73 (sauced shrimp to closer sauced shrimp) and 11.53 (macro to macro). These read as a continuous transformation rather than jumps.
study.effects: Warm, saturated colour grade that pushes reds and oranges; the glaze looks almost neon red-orange from ~5s onward. Contrast is high, blacks are deep in the griddle and background, and there's noticeable sharpening/clarity on shell texture and seasoning granules. Optical shallow depth-of-field blur is used everywhere. There are no zooms added in editing (the movement is handheld drift), no shakes, flashes, split screens or freeze frames.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264 at ~5.3 Mbps, which is adequate but not 4K-sharp. The high-end feel comes from the shooting rather than the resolution: macro framing, very shallow depth of field, warm directional light making specular highlights on the sauce, and a steady handheld camera with only slow drift. Exposure is controlled with no blown highlights on the glossy shells. The commercial griddle, steel hood and branded sauce bottle say restaurant kitchen. Minor softness and compression show in the blurred areas.
study.ending: It ends on the money shot: the 4.27s macro hold of the finished glossy crusted shrimp bubbling on the griddle, with no bite, reaction or CTA. The last cut is at 11.53s and the video runs 4.27s more. Because it opens and ends on the same kind of shot (macro of shrimp sizzling in butter on the griddle), it loops almost seamlessly from cooked back to raw.
study.why_viral: 1) A clear colour transformation in 15s, from pale pink in butter to dusted orange to lacquered glossy red, so viewers watch to see the result. 2) Extreme macro at griddle level with shallow focus makes shrimp look huge and textural (bubbles, seasoning granules, sauce gloss), triggering appetite without needing sound. 3) Satisfying action beats (falling seasoning, a thin golden pour, spatula tosses) cut at ~1.4s keep it moving, and the long final hold lets the craving land. 4) The seamless loop and a trending warm song boost rewatches.
lessons: Shoot the hero ingredient at griddle or plate level with a macro lens a few cm away, and fill at least 80% of the vertical frame with food. Keep the background a neutral dark surface so the food's colour pops.

Structure short process clips as a visible colour or texture transformation (raw → seasoned → sauced → finished) and show each stage in its own 1–1.8s shot from the same angle, so the cuts read like match cuts.
Keep process shots at 0.9–1.8s (median ~1.4s, ~5–6 cuts per 10s), then give the finished dish one hold 2–3x longer than any other shot (here 4.27s, starting ~73% into the video).
Snap the first 3–4 cuts exactly to music hits (within ~0.05s); after that you can loosen the timing so it doesn't feel mechanical.
Slow seasoning drops and thin pours to roughly 50% speed when the footage allows, because suspended particles and droplets read as premium. Leave tossing and spatula action at real speed for energy.
Open on food already in motion (bubbling butter, sizzle) with no text in the first 2s, and end on the same type of shot as the opener so the video loops.
Grade warm with boosted red/orange saturation and deep blacks, and add mild sharpening on texture. Avoid blowing out highlights on glossy sauces.
Keep hands out of frame and let only the tools enter, and place a branded sauce bottle or logo item softly blurred in the background (as at 8.0s) for subtle branding instead of a text CTA.

study.format: POV meme-caption montage: a handheld walk-in through the shop door, then a fast reel of dessert close-ups (product showcase / menu reveal hybrid). There is no speech.
study.item: Dessert crêpes and sweets from a crêpe shop: a crêpe piped with alternating chocolate-hazelnut and pistachio-cream ridges and buried under crushed pistachios; mini pancakes (poffertjes-style) topped with strawberries and banana under chocolate and white-chocolate zigzags; a takeout box of crêpe with a feathered chocolate/white-chocolate marble pattern, a whipped-cream rosette, bananas and strawberries; a clear cup of chocolate-coated crêpe pieces with a bright green (pistachio/matcha-style) drizzle. The visual pull comes from strong color contrast (green-on-brown, red berries on golden dough), glossy sauce sheen and graphic piped or feathered patterns.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0–0.6s) is a shaky handheld POV at the shop's glass door. There are payment and chamber stickers on the glass and a white orchid arch with purple and blue balloons visible through it. A two-line white caption sits mid-frame from the first frame: 'how my brain feels walking into my favorite dessert shop'. The music's strongest hits land at 0.32s and 0.75s. The scroll-stopper is the relatable meme caption, not the food. It sets up a promise of what's inside, and the door-opening POV puts the viewer in the creator's shoes. The pretty flower-and-balloon entrance signals an 'aesthetic' spot before any food appears.

beats.what: POV approaching the glass door, which has stickers and an orchid arch visible inside; the meme caption is already on screen.
Jump cut to a hand gripping the door handle and pulling it open. The camera walks in past the white orchid and balloon arch and a green grass wall (2.63s, the longest shot).
Pan across the interior toward the wood-paneled counter and display cases.
Hard cut to an extreme close-up of a scoop raining crushed pistachios onto a crêpe striped with chocolate-hazelnut and pistachio cream.
The finished pistachio crêpe is held almost still: a glossy brown/green ridged pattern against a white plate.
Rack focus from a fully blurred frame into mini pancakes topped with strawberries and banana under chocolate and white zigzags.
Tighter, sharper angle on the same mini-pancake plate, gliding across the berries.
Black takeout box on a yellow cloth: a whipped-cream rosette next to a feather-marbled chocolate/white-chocolate crêpe, with the camera sliding along the pattern.
The same box from another angle, showing banana slices and strawberries tucked behind the marbled crêpe.
A clear cup of chocolate-coated crêpe pieces gets a thin stream of bright green sauce drizzled over it. The video ends on this pour (cut point estimated; see transitions).

study.how_food_is_shown: The opening 4s are a handheld eye-level POV walking in, with natural daylight at the door and fluorescent ceiling light inside. From 4.0s the food shots switch to a low, near-table-level macro at roughly 15–30° with very shallow depth of field, so the background melts to soft grey/white. The pistachio crêpe and mini pancakes sit on white plates against a white/grey backdrop, with bright, even, soft daylight-style light and small specular highlights on the sauce. The takeout-box shots (7.93–9.27s) are a little higher at about 45° on a yellow cloth and feel more like phone footage, with flatter light. The final cup shot is again low and macro, with the plastic cup rim in the foreground. Hands appear only in the door shots; the food shots show at most a scoop or a sauce stream. The emphasis is on color contrast (pistachio green vs chocolate brown, red berries vs golden batter, white whipped cream vs black box) and on gloss and texture in the piped ridges, feathered marble and crushed nuts.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 4.0–~4.5s: extreme close-up of crushed pistachios tumbling from a scoop onto the crêpe (visible in the frame just after the cut). It plays at roughly normal speed, possibly slightly slowed, and fills the left half of the frame. 4.5–6.0s: macro of the piped chocolate/pistachio ridges, slowly revealing the nut pile on the left. Motion drops to 8.3 around 5.0–5.5s, a near-still hold of about 0.5–1s. 6.0–6.87s: rack focus from completely blurred to sharp on the mini pancakes and strawberries, very close (berries fill the frame). 6.87–7.93s: glide across the drizzled pancakes. 7.93–9.27s: macro slide along the feathered chocolate/white marble beside the whipped-cream rosette. ~9.8–10.9s: a thin, smooth green sauce stream drizzles into the cup over the chocolate crêpe. Motion is only 9.4–13.9 here, a calm and possibly slowed pour held about 1.1s to the end.
study.money_shot: The green drizzle pour into the chocolate crêpe cup lands around 9.8s (~90% through) and is held about 1.1s until the video ends at 10.9s. The shot has the lowest motion of the food section, so the eye locks onto the sauce stream. It is set up by a quick escalation of increasingly saucy close-ups (pistachio crêpe, then drizzled pancakes, then marbled box), and nothing follows it: the video ends on the pour. A close runner-up is the pistachio sprinkle at 4.0s (37%), which serves as the first food payoff right after the walk-in.
study.pacing: The video has two speeds. The walk-in section (0–4.0s) has 3 shots of 0.6s, 2.63s and 0.77s, letting the POV breathe and build anticipation. The food section (4.0–10.9s) has 5 detected shots of 2.0s, 0.87s, 1.07s, 1.33s and 1.63s, plus likely one more cut inside the last shot. The median shot is 1.2s, with 6.42 cuts per 10s overall. The longest food hold (2.0s, pistachio crêpe) comes first, then the shots shorten to about 1s each, so the reveal feels like a rapid 'everything on the menu' scroll. Motion peaks at 44.3 at 1.5s (door swing) and 53.4 at 9.0s (camera move and cut into the final dish), then settles to 9–14 on the closing pour. The first cut at 0.6s sits between the audio hits at 0.32s and 0.75s; the other cut timings can't be confirmed against the beat from the data given.
study.speed: No timelapses or obvious speed ramps. The food shots are smooth and low-motion. The green drizzle at ~9.8–10.9s (motion 9.4–13.9) reads as possibly mild slow motion or simply a slow, steady pour (low confidence). The pistachio sprinkle at 4.0s plays at about normal or slightly slowed speed (low confidence). The walk-in POV plays at normal speed.
study.on_screen_text: One meme caption for the whole video: 'how my brain feels walking into my favorite dessert shop'. It is all lowercase, in a regular-weight white sans-serif (TikTok-style), with a thin dark drop shadow and no box. It sits in two centered lines just above the vertical middle (about 48–52% down), is visible from 0s to the end, and shows all 10 words at once. There are no item names or prices.
study.audio: There is no speech or voiceover. The soundtrack is a music track with its strongest hits at 0.32s, 0.75s and 1.15s, clustered in the opening hook during the door approach and opening. No distinct ASMR sounds (sizzle, pour or crunch) can be confirmed; the food shots appear to rely on the music.
study.transitions: Hard cuts only. Details: a jump cut at 0.6s from the approach to the hand on the handle; a hard cut at 3.23s within the walk-in; a hard cut at 4.0s from the interior wide to the food macro, the key shift from 'place' to 'food'. At 6.0s the cut lands on a fully blurred frame that racks into focus, which works like a soft focus-pull transition. Hard cuts follow at 6.87s, 7.93s and 9.27s. Frames at 9.39s (marbled box) and 9.99s (green-drizzle cup) show different dishes inside the last detected shot, and motion spikes to 53.4 near 9.0–9.5s. This suggests an extra undetected cut or fast whip around 9.5–9.8s.
study.effects: Rack focus from full blur to sharp at 6.0–6.5s. The shallow depth-of-field background blur in the food shots is in-camera, not a post effect. The food clips have a bright, slightly lifted, clean grade with neutral whites and saturated greens and reds, while the door and box footage looks flatter and more phone-like, which suggests mixed sources. No zoom effects, shakes, freeze frames or split screens.
study.quality: Delivered at 480x854, 30fps, about 2.3 Mbps H.264, so it is soft overall and shows compression in fine detail (stickers, orchids). The walk-in is shaky handheld phone footage with fluorescent interior light, which feels authentic and homemade. The plated food shots are clearly higher-end: stable, macro, with shallow depth of field, soft even light and a clean white background, so the gloss on the sauces and the crumble of the pistachios read well even at low resolution. The takeout-box clips sit in between: flatter light and a busier yellow background. The polish of the food clips is what makes the desserts look premium despite the low delivery resolution.
study.ending: It ends mid-pour on the green drizzle cup about 1.1s after that shot starts, with no CTA, reaction or end card. Because it cuts on an in-progress pour, it feels unfinished and loops naturally back to the door-opening POV.
study.why_viral: The relatable meme caption ('how my brain feels walking into…') turns a shop ad into a feeling viewers share and tag friends with. The walk-in POV builds 4s of anticipation, then hard-cuts to macro food: a clear 'door, then dopamine' payoff. Four different desserts in 7s at about 1s each feels like an overwhelming menu, which matches the 'my brain' joke. Bold color contrasts (pistachio green on chocolate, red berries, feathered marble) and live pours and sprinkles make each shot instantly crave-worthy.
lessons: Open with a relatable meme-style text hook ('how my brain feels walking into…'), 8–12 lowercase words in white with a soft shadow, centered just above mid-frame, and keep it on for the entire video so there's nothing else to read.
Use 3–4s of POV entrance footage (door handle, decor, counter) before any food to build anticipation, then hard-cut to an extreme food macro, ideally one with motion like a sprinkle or pour.
Give the first food shot the longest hold (~2s), then speed up to ~0.9–1.3s per dish so the reveal feels like an overwhelming menu.
Lead every dish shot with an action (nuts raining down, sauce drizzling) or a rack focus from full blur to sharp; static plates should be under 1s.
Shoot food low (15–30°) and close with shallow depth of field against a plain white or grey background so sauce gloss and color contrast pop, even at 480p.
Pick hero items with strong color contrast (green vs brown, red berries vs golden batter, white cream vs black box) and graphic patterns like piped ridges or feathered drizzle.
End on the calmest, slowest pour (motion around 10) and cut while it's still pouring, under ~1.5s into the shot, so the video loops instead of resolving.
Use one music track with hits in the first second and land the first cut (~0.6s) between hits to make the opening feel snappy; no voiceover is needed.

study.format: Making-of / process montage for a food truck pop-up, set to music: night queue, then griddle prep, assembly line, then pickup-window handoff
study.item: Smash burgers from a night-time food truck (the lit menu board reads 'Smash Burgers – Limited Run', $10). The visual hooks are billowing steam as patties are smashed on a flat-top, bright yellow American cheese melting into glossy pools over lacy crusted edges, rows of foam clamshells with toasted buns and sauce, and a long line of customers in the dark.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0–0.9s) is a dark parking lot with a long line of hooded people queued toward a glowing orange menu board and food truck. On the first sound (0.08s) the lyric 'Somebody's watching me' kicks in. It stops the scroll through social proof (why are all these people lined up at night?), a moody high-contrast night look, and a recognizable, slightly ominous song. The cut at 0.9s to a second angle of the crowd lands near the 1.15s audio hit.

beats.what: Night wide shot of a long line in a parking lot leading to the lit food truck; 'Somebody's watching me' lyric starts.
Second angle of the dark queue, people shuffling.
Closer on the truck: street lamp, glowing menu board 'Smash Burgers – Limited Run $10', rainbow lens flare.
Crowd pressed at the truck window, heavy blue light and rainbow flare (cut lands on 2.76s hit).
Inside: gloved hand slams the smasher onto patties on the flat-top, backlit steam billowing (longest shot, 2.23s).
Cheese slices laid onto patties through smoke, warm red-orange glow.
Row of cheesed patties steaming on the griddle, cheese starting to slump.
Macro: spatula scoops a cheesy patty, cheese draping and melting, steam.
Red squeeze bottle zigzags sauce onto toasted buns in a long row of clamshells.
Hands moving down the line of open boxes with sauced buns.
Low wide of the clamshell row, then a gloved hand drops a cheese-topped patty into a box.
Macro low-angle on a patty in its box: glossy, glistening yellow cheese over crusty lacy edges, shallow depth of field, near-still hold.
Second macro of the melted cheese patty with more patties dropping in behind.
Row of boxes now filled with molten-cheese patties, hand adding more.
Hand places another patty; low angle down the full assembly line.
High angle down the row of loaded boxes with an orange/pink light-leak wash.
Long row of completed open boxes (cheesy patties plus sauced buns) receding into depth: the scale shot.
Pickup window with red 'PICK UP HERE' sign; hooded worker grabs a bagged order.
Bag lifted toward the customer, rainbow flare across the frame.
Bag held out through the window.
Bag handed to the customer at the window (implicit 'come get one'); ends.

study.how_food_is_shown: Almost all food shots are low, near counter-level, eye-level-to-griddle or 30–45° angles with long lenses and very shallow depth of field, so foreground cheese is sharp and the receding row of boxes melts into bokeh. Gloved hands are in frame for nearly every food shot (smasher, spatula, squeeze bottle, placing patties), which signals craft and handmade work. Lighting is hard backlight through steam on the griddle (steam glows white), warm red/orange heat-lamp tones on the cheese, and clean white foam clamshells as a neutral backdrop that makes the yellow cheese and brown crust pop. Color emphasis: saturated yellow cheese, browned lacy crust, red sauce. Repetition and scale come from lines of identical boxes shot down their length. Bookend scenes are dark night exteriors with point light sources and rainbow flares.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 3.83–6.07s: medium-close smash on the griddle, held 2.23s, steam backlit and swirling smoothly (likely mild slow motion). 6.07–7.13s: close on cheese being laid on patties through smoke, ~1.07s. 7.13–8.97s: close of the steaming cheesed patties, 1.83s. 8.97–9.93s: macro of the spatula lifting a cheesy patty, cheese draping, ~0.97s. 9.93–11.83s: the drizzle, a red squeeze bottle laying sauce lines onto buns, held 1.9s at close range with the bottle filling the left of frame. 13.03–13.73s: gloved hand pressing a cheesy patty into a box, close. 13.73–15.5s: extreme macro on glossy melted cheese over a crusty patty, 1.77s, nearly still (motion drops to 6.1 at 14.5s). 15.5–16.5s: second macro of the same cheese texture, 1.0s. 16.5–19.0s: close-to-medium shots of molten cheese patties in boxes as hands add more. No cheese pull or bite.
study.money_shot: The extreme macro of glistening, molten yellow cheese slumped over a crusty smashed patty in its clamshell, 13.73–16.5s (~54–65% of the video). The first shot is held 1.77s at near-zero motion, followed by a 1.0s second macro. It is set up by the steam/smash and cheese-on-griddle sequence (3.83–9.93s), which shows the melt being created, then the sauce drizzle and the hand dropping the patty into the box just before it. It is followed by the pull-back scale shots of the full row of loaded boxes (16.5–21.07s).
study.pacing: Fast and even. 21 shots in 25.3s (7.91 cuts/10s), median shot 1.07s, range 0.7s to 2.23s. Opening crowd shots run ~0.9–1.07s each for a snappy hook. The single longest hold (2.23s) goes to the steam smash, and longer holds of 1.77–1.9s go to the key food textures (steaming griddle, sauce drizzle, cheese macro). Assembly and handoff shots return to ~0.8–1.3s. Many cuts land on audio hits: 2.77 (hit 2.76), 8.97 (9.02), 11.83 (11.81), 16.5 (16.45), 19.0 (18.92), 20.07 (19.91), 24.33 (24.16). Rhythm stays steady with no breathing pause; the structure is crowd → cook → assemble → handoff.
study.speed: Likely gentle real slow motion (moderate confidence) on the griddle shots 3.83–9.93s: steam rolls smoothly and slowly while hands move, and motion stays mostly 15–30 with spikes from hand movement rather than jumpy change. The cheese macros at 13.73–16.5s play as a near-still slow hold (motion 6.1 at 14.5s), probably slowed or a very slow push. No timelapse or obvious speed ramp within a shot. The night crowd and pickup shots play at normal speed (handheld).
study.on_screen_text: none. The only words visible are physical signage in the scene: the menu board ('Smash Burgers – Limited Run', $10) at ~2s and the red 'PICK UP HERE' sign at 21–25s.
study.audio: A music track built on the hook lyric 'Somebody's watching me' (only 3 words, 0.08–1.66s). The song carries the whole video; there is no voiceover and no audible ASMR sizzle as a separate element. The track's strong hits drive the edit: cuts sit on or within ~0.15s of hits at 2.76, 9.02, 11.81, 16.45, 18.92, 19.91 and 24.16s. The 'watching' lyric plays off the crowd staring at the truck.
study.transitions: Hard cuts only, with no whips or wipes. Several are motion-matched (steam smash → cheese drop, macro → macro of the same patty at 15.5s) so the flow feels continuous. Some light-leak/flare washes sit across cuts at 3.83s and around 19s but are overlays, not transitions.
study.effects: Rainbow prism/lens-flare arcs on the night shots (1.8–3.83s) and the pickup shots (22.33–25.3s), either a prism filter or an added flare effect, fairly strong. An orange-pink light-leak wash over the assembly row at ~19.0–20.07s. A warm, saturated grade on the food (boosted yellows and oranges, warm reds on the griddle) with crushed blacks and contrast. The night shots are dark with lifted highlights. Slow push-ins on the cheese macros. Mild sharpening. No split screens or freeze frames.
study.quality: 720×1280, 30fps, 5744 kbps h264, so modest resolution but a decent bitrate. Kitchen footage looks pro: stable (gimbal or tripod), shallow depth of field from a long lens or fast prime, clean exposure, backlit steam. The night exteriors are handheld, noisy and soft, which reads as authentic 'you had to be there' crowd footage. Contrast between a raw street vibe and cinematic food close-ups makes the burgers feel premium while the event feels real.
study.ending: Ends on the customer receiving the bagged order at the 'PICK UP HERE' window (24.33–25.3s, last shot 0.97s), with the rainbow flare still on screen. It cuts right after the hand-off begins, with no lingering. The night exterior bookends the opening crowd shot, so it loops cleanly back to the queue.
study.why_viral: 1) Social-proof hook: a long nighttime line plus the 'Somebody's watching me' lyric makes viewers curious about what everyone is waiting for. 2) Sensory escalation from the steam smash to melting cheese to an extreme macro of glossy molten cheese on crusty edges, the classic smash-burger craving trigger. 3) Scale and scarcity: endless rows of identical boxes and a 'Limited Run' menu board read as a hyped, sold-out pop-up. 4) Tight beat-synced editing (~1s shots) with a cinematic warm grade keeps it rewatchable and loopable.
lessons: Open on social proof, not food: a 0.9–1s wide of a line or crowd, synced to the first lyric or beat, buys the first 2 seconds and makes the food feel worth waiting for.
Keep median shot length near 1s for hype content, but give the 1–2 key texture moments (smash with steam, cheese macro) 1.8–2.2s holds so they register.
Backlight steam and smoke: put the light source behind the griddle so steam glows. It reads as heat and freshness even without sound.
Shoot the melt in extreme macro at a low angle with shallow depth of field, and hold it nearly still (motion near zero) at about 55–65% of the runtime as the payoff.
Show scale by shooting down the length of a repeated row (boxes, plates, cups) at counter height so the far end falls into bokeh; use 2–3 of these after the money shot.
Cut on the music's hits: aim for cuts within ~0.15s of strong beats, especially at section changes (exterior → kitchen → assembly → pickup).
Keep gloved hands in nearly every food shot (pressing, drizzling, placing) to convey craft and motion, so every shot has an action.
Grade food warm and saturated (push yellows and oranges, deepen blacks) and leave exteriors moody; a light leak or prism flare at the bookends adds atmosphere without touching the food.
Bookend with the customer handoff at the window so the story closes (line → food → you get it) and loops back to the opening crowd.

study.format: Making-of / drink build. A café barista assembles a signature seasonal iced coffee from espresso shot to finished glass, set to music with no voice. It ends on a hero shot of the drink on a table in the café.
study.item: 'Salty Springs', Shibam Coffee's spring drink. It is an iced shaken espresso: espresso, caramel sauce and cream are built in a shaker on a scale, with a pink Himalayan salt bottle in frame. The mix is shaken and poured into a branded clear can-glass that is pre-lined with caramel streaks over ice. Milk goes in next, then a thick white cold-foam cap, then a round golden cracker/biscuit on top finished with a caramel drizzle. What makes it visual: amber caramel 'tiger' drips running down clear glass, coffee marbling into milk, a distinct white foam layer, and a glossy caramel string falling onto the topper.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0-0.43s) is an eye-level shot of a shiny chrome espresso machine pulling two thin amber streams into a steel shot pitcher. The bold title 'SALTY SPRINGS' is already animating in at center screen. At 0.43s a warm orange/white light-leak flash hits, synced to audio hits at 0.31 and 0.77s, and the full title lands: 'SALTY SPRINGS' over 'SHIBAM COFFEE SPRING DRINK'. It stops the scroll because the espresso stream reads instantly as 'coffee being made'. The glowing flash plus the named drink frame it as a menu launch, and the brand name tells you where to buy it.

beats.what: Espresso streams into a steel pitcher at eye level; title animates in.
Same espresso shot washed with a warm light-leak flash; 'SALTY SPRINGS / SHIBAM COFFEE SPRING DRINK' fully on screen.
Tighter, lower angle on the twin espresso streams with chrome reflections; title held until 3.4s.
Caramel sauce squeezed into a measuring shaker on a scale, then a cream stream (~3.9s), then espresso poured from the pitcher with the pink Himalayan salt bottle beside it (~4.6s).
Through a white/yellow flash: close shot of the mixed coffee base in the shaker on the scale.
Fast, blurry close-up of ice going into the shaker.
Gloved barista shakes the sealed shaker high in front of the café's gold decor (cut on audio hit 6.87).
Shaking continues (cut on hit ~7.81), then caramel is squeezed into the branded glass full of ice (~9.5s).
Handheld frother whips milk beside the now caramel-streaked branded glass.
Shaken caramel coffee poured into the glass over ice and the caramel drips.
Milk streams in and marbles through the amber coffee.
Thick cold foam slides out of the pitcher and caps the drink.
Domed white foam layer held on top of the amber layers.
Gloved fingers set a round golden cracker on the foam and hold it in place (~20-23.6s).
Glossy caramel string drizzled onto the cracker and foam, pooling and dripping over the rim edge.
Torn-paper transition into the finished drink on a white marble café table.
Slow handheld drift/orbit reveals the 'Shibam Coffee Co.' sign behind the drink, with prism light flares; video ends here.

study.how_food_is_shown: Almost everything is shot eye-level or slightly low, at counter height. The glass fills about 60-80% of the vertical frame, so the caramel drips, coffee/milk marbling and foam layer read as stacked bands. The camera is close and handheld, and black-gloved hands are in frame for nearly every prep beat, which signals hygiene and a pro bar. Lighting is the café's own warm interior light plus daylight from windows. Chrome on the espresso machine and gold wall decor give sparkle and warm highlights. The branded can-glass with the 'Shibam Coffee Co.' logo is always turned to camera, so the product and brand appear together. Props tell the story: the scale with its ml markings, the salt bottle and the caramel squeeze bottle. The final shot moves to a clean white marble table with tan chairs, reading as 'served to you'. Color emphasis throughout is amber/orange caramel against white foam and clear glass.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0-3.4s: espresso twin-stream pour, held 3.4s over 3 shots at medium-close, normal or near-normal speed. 3.4-5.1s: caramel squeeze, cream stream and espresso-pitcher pour into the shaker, quick and ~0.5s each. 5.97-6.87s: very close, motion-blurred ice drop into the shaker. ~9.5-10.6s: close-up of caramel squeezed into the glass over ice, ~1s. 13.0-14.5s: shaken coffee poured over the caramel-lined glass, ~1.5s, the glass filling the frame. 15.1-15.9s: milk stream marbling into the coffee, ~0.8s. 16.5-18.0s: thick cold-foam ribbon slowly folding onto the drink, ~1.5s, close (glass fills the frame); the motion is smooth and low (6.7-11.3), which may be mild slow motion. 20.0-23.6s: cracker placed on the foam, held ~3.6s with almost no motion (2.7-5.7). 23.87-28.3s: caramel drizzle onto the cracker, a long ~4.4s hold, close, the stream smooth and glossy; motion 5.2-8.7, possibly slightly slowed.
study.money_shot: The caramel drizzle onto the cracker-topped foam lands at 23.87s, about 71% through, and is held about 4.4s until ~28.3s (about 84%). It is set up by the cracker placement at 20-23.6s, which is a nearly still hold that makes the viewer wait for the finishing touch. Before that come the foam pour (16.5-18s) and the foam dome reveal (18.6s), so each layer builds toward the topping. It is followed by a torn-paper transition into the finished hero shot on the café table (28.5-33.8s). The cold-foam pour at 16.5-18s (49-53%) is the secondary big moment.
study.pacing: The structure has two halves. Fast first third: 8 cuts in 10.67s, with shots of 0.43, 0.9, 2.07, 1.73, 0.83, 0.9, 1.0 and 2.8s. That covers the espresso, shaker build, ice and shaking, with motion mostly 20-48. Several cuts land on music hits: 0.43 (~0.31/0.77), 1.33 (1.25), 3.4 (3.36), 6.87 (6.87), 7.87 (7.81). Slow second two-thirds: two long detected shots of 13.2s and 9.93s. Inside them are soft, dissolve-like changes at ~12.5, ~14.5, ~16 and ~19.5s, visible as small motion bumps of 16-23. Those bumps split the assembly into 1.5-3.5s pours. Holds get longer as the drink nears completion: cracker 3.6s, drizzle 4.4s, hero 5.3s. Median motion is only 8.5, and the second half sits at 3-9. The rhythm is energetic prep, then ASMR-like calm for the pours and garnish.
study.speed: Mostly real-time. The shaking at 6.87-9.5s plays at normal speed (motion 22-48). The cold-foam pour (16.5-18s) and the caramel drizzle (23.87-28.3s) look smooth with low motion (5-11) and may be mildly slowed (~0.5-0.75x). That is moderate-to-low confidence, since the streams look natural at 30fps. No timelapse and no obvious speed ramps.
study.on_screen_text: One title card. Line 1 is 'SALTY SPRINGS' in a heavy white uppercase geometric sans with a slight shadow. Below it is a thin white rule, then 'SHIBAM COFFEE SPRING DRINK' in light, wide-tracked white uppercase. The card is centered at about 47-53% of frame height.
