It animates in from ~0.3s (mid-reveal at 0.35s, complete by ~0.43s) and stays through the light-leak flash until the cut at 3.4s, about 3s total, 6 words. No prices and no other text. The caption-style watermark is ignored as platform/branding overlay.
study.audio: No speech or voiceover. A music track carries the video, with hits clustering at the start (0.31, 0.77, 1.25, 1.7). A rapid run at 3.12-4.29 (~0.23s apart) drives the fast shaker-prep cuts. Further hits at 6.87 and 7.81 match the cuts into and within the shaking. The hits are sparser in the slow half (13.4-14.8 during the coffee pour, 16.7 at the foam pour, 22.96, 24.89/25.33 during the drizzle, 28.88 at the torn-paper transition, 30.97 on the hero). No natural ASMR sound can be confirmed from the data; the edit relies on the music.
study.transitions: 0.43: hard cut combined with a warm orange light-leak flash. 1.33: hard cut through a bright white/yellow flash (overexposed frames). 3.4: hard cut on a beat. 5.13: flash/light-leak transition, with the frame going almost fully white-yellow before the cut. 5.97 and 6.87: fast motion-blurred cuts, almost whip-like, on the ice and shaking. 7.87: hard cut (jump within the shaking). Inside the 10.67-23.87 shot: soft dissolves or blended cuts at ~12.5-13, ~14.5-15, ~16-16.5 and ~19.5-20, which cut detection missed. 23.87: hard cut to the drizzle. ~28.3-28.5: torn-paper graphic wipe, with ripped white paper edges and a small brown diamond shape, revealing the hero table shot.
study.effects: Warm light-leak/flash overlays at 0.43-1.33s and ~5.1s. Recurring rainbow prism/lens-flare overlays drift across the frame at ~3.9s, 10.2s, 13.7s, 18.0s, 25.7s, 30.6s and 32.7s, adding sparkle. The grade is warm and saturated, pushing the orange/amber caramel and keeping the foam bright white, with moderate contrast. There is a torn-paper graphic at 28.5s. The hero shot has a slow handheld drift/push revealing the café sign. No freeze frames or split screens.
study.quality: 720x1280 vertical, 30fps, ~5.9 Mbps h264. Shot on a phone, handheld throughout, with visible motion blur in the 5.97-7.87s ice and shake shots and some soft focus. Exposure is bright, sometimes blown out on purpose by the flashes. The professional feel comes from the setting rather than the camera: chrome machine, gold decor, gloved hands, clean marble counter, branded glassware, and a calm second half where the glass stays centered and steady. Resolution is modest, but the warm grade, prism flares and clean layer separation make it look polished.
study.ending: Ends on the finished drink on a marble table in the dining room. The camera slowly drifts to reveal the 'Shibam Coffee Co.' wall sign behind it, held about 5.3s (28.5-33.8s), with prism flares. It ends about 5.5s after the last drizzle beat. A motion spike of 43 at ~33.5s suggests the clip was trimmed mid-move. It doesn't loop cleanly back to the espresso opening.
study.why_viral: 1) Visible layering in a clear glass: caramel tiger drips, coffee marbling into milk, then a thick white foam cap. Each pour visibly changes the drink, so viewers stay to see the next layer. 2) A satisfying build sequence: espresso, then shaker, then shake, then pour, then foam, then topper, then drizzle. The slow, held cold-foam pour and caramel drizzle are near-ASMR. 3) A named, seasonal, limited-feeling drink ('Salty Springs', 'spring drink'), with the brand on the glass and the café sign in the final shot. That turns appetite into a 'go try it' intent. 4) Fast, beat-synced cuts with flashes in the first 10s keep energy high before the calmer payoff.
lessons: Open on an instantly readable process shot (espresso stream, pour, sizzle) and land the drink's name as bold text within 0.5s. Keep it to 6 words or fewer and hold it about 3s.
Split the edit in two: quick prep cuts of 0.4-1s synced to music hits for the first ~30%, then long holds of 3-5s for pours, foam and garnish.
Put the clear glass at eye level and let it fill 60-80% of frame height, so every layer and drip reads as a horizontal band.
Hold the final garnish and drizzle as the money shot for at least 4s at around 70-85% of the runtime. Set it up with a near-still beat (like placing the topper) just before.
Pre-line glassware with sauce drips before the pour. It makes every following pour more visual and photographs far better than a plain glass.
Turn the branded cup or logo to camera in every assembly shot, and end on a 4-6s hero shot in the dining room with the shop sign visible.
Use flash or light-leak transitions only on 2-3 early cuts to add energy, and drop them once the pours start so the food stays readable.
Show gloved hands, scales and real ingredients (salt bottle, sauce bottle). These cues signal a craft, professional bar and justify a specialty-drink price.
Cut rapid motion (shaking, ice) on audio hits. Keep the slow pours smooth, and optionally slow them to 0.5-0.75x if the footage is shot at 60fps or higher.

study.format: Making-of / assembly process set to a trending audio clip, in a 'pov: us whenever we make…' meme framing, shot in a dessert shop
study.item: Dubai chocolate strawberry cup: a clear plastic cup packed with fresh cut strawberries, buried under glossy milk-chocolate zig-zags, then bright pistachio-green cream drizzle, golden toasted kataifi shreds and a heap of crushed pistachios. The visual hook is the color stacking: red, then glossy brown, then neon green, then gold, then pale green. The see-through cup also shows the layers inside.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0-0.77s) is an eye-level macro of wet, glistening red strawberry halves in a clear cup, softly lit against a bright white background. A chocolate nozzle is already dipping into the top of the frame (visible just before the 0.77s cut). The audio opens on the first word, 'I'm in love' at 0.00s, a recognizable trending sound. The white lowercase text 'pov: us whenever we make a dubai chocolate strawberry cup' names the viral trend item instantly. Trend name, fresh red fruit and an incoming chocolate pour all land inside the first second, so the viewer knows a drizzle is coming.

beats.what: Macro of fresh strawberries in a clear cup, chocolate nozzle entering frame, 'I'm in love' plus trend-naming POV text
Melted chocolate starts piping onto the strawberries, nozzle at top left
Longest shot (3.07s): thick glossy chocolate zig-zags fall over the fruit as a thin stream, then the camera drifts back to show the cup's side layers (~3.3-4.0s)
Close-up of the fully chocolate-coated top; green pistachio cream starts falling in at the end of the shot (cut lands on the 4.31s audio hit)
Neon-green pistachio drizzle lines laid over glossy brown chocolate, held 2.57s with very little motion
0.43s out-of-focus flash of the cup now covered in golden kataifi, racking into focus
Kataifi topping in focus, loose shreds and bits still settling, 1.9s
Crushed pistachios tumble from a scoop at top of frame and pile onto the cup
Fast pull-back/tilt to the side of the finished cup showing strawberries, chocolate, green drizzle and pistachio layers through the plastic (motion spikes to 89.6 at 12.0s)

study.how_food_is_shown: Nearly every shot is a low, eye-level-to-slight-45° macro, only centimetres from the cup rim. The rim of the clear cup frames the bottom of the shot and the toppings fill the middle. Hands never appear; only the nozzle, squeeze bottle and pistachio scoop enter from the top edge, which keeps the food the hero. The background is a bright, blown-out white/grey shop interior with a dark blurred bottle shape, giving shallow depth of field. Lighting is soft, even, cool-neutral daylight that throws hard specular highlights on the chocolate and pistachio cream, so the sauces read as wet and glossy. Composition stays the same across all shots (strawberry tip upper-left, cup rim lower third), so each new layer reads as a clear 'before/after'. Color emphasis comes from complementary contrast: red against brown against green, then gold and pale green crumbs.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0.77-1.27s: chocolate pour begins, macro, ~0.5s, normal speed. 1.27-4.33s: continuous chocolate zig-zag drizzle in extreme close-up; the thin falling stream is visible at 2.1-2.7s and the glossy ridges build up. Held 3.07s, normal speed, ending with a slow drift that reveals the cup's side layers. 4.33-5.23s: tight close-up of the glossy chocolate top, green drizzle entering. 5.23-7.8s: pistachio cream drizzle in macro, lines stacked across the chocolate, held 2.57s, the calmest stretch (motion 5.7 at 6.0s). 7.8-8.23s: blurred kataifi frame racking into focus. 8.23-10.13s: kataifi close-up with stray shreds falling and settling. 10.13-12.1s: crushed pistachio cascade from a scoop, pieces motion-blurred mid-air, ~1.5s. It is possibly very slightly slowed, but most likely normal speed (low confidence). It finishes with a pull-out to the side profile of the cup.
study.money_shot: The pistachio-green drizzle over glossy chocolate at 5.23-7.8s, landing ~43% into the video and held 2.57s, the second-longest shot. It is set up by 3+ seconds of brown chocolate building up, so the sudden neon green over brown is a color pop. The cut into it lands just after the 5.03s audio hit. It is followed by quick texture layers (kataifi, pistachio crumble), then the full-cup reveal as the final payoff.
study.pacing: Mixed. Fast 0.5-0.9s cuts mark the start of each new topping (0.77, 0.5, 0.9, 0.43s). Longer 1.9-3.07s holds let the satisfying pours play out: chocolate 3.07s, green drizzle 2.57s, kataifi 1.9s, pistachio 1.97s. That is 8 shots in 12.1s, 5.79 cuts per 10s, median shot 1.4s. Median motion is moderate (17.4), with peaks at the cuts (40.6 at 1.0s, 41.6 at 5.0s) and a final 89.6 spike on the closing camera move. Cuts loosely follow the audio: the 4.33 cut sits on the 4.31 hit, 0.77/1.27 bracket 'love'/'I'm', and 7.8 is near the 8.0 hit. The structure is one shot per layer, so the video moves like a build-up checklist.
study.speed: Mostly normal speed. The chocolate and green drizzles play in real time; streams fall naturally and no smooth slow-mo is evident. The pistachio cascade at 10.2-11.5s may be slightly slowed (soft, blurry falling pieces), low confidence. There are no timelapses and no clear speed ramps. The final 0.5s motion spike (89.6) reads as a quick camera pull-back/whip toward the full-cup profile, not a speed effect.
study.on_screen_text: One line for the entire 12.1s: 'pov: us whenever we make a dubai chocolate strawberry cup'. It is set in all-lowercase, regular-weight white sans-serif (TikTok classic style) with a subtle dark shadow, centered over two lines in the upper third (~y 22-28%), above the food. That is 10 words at once, static, with no prices.
study.captions: none (the spoken trending audio is not captioned; the POV text does the framing)
study.audio: Trending voice clip 'I'm in love, I'm obsessed, and I don't even feel guilty about it' from 0.00-4.40s, then a music bed carries the rest (audio hits roughly every 0.3-0.6s through 12s). The words match the picture emotionally: 'obsessed' over the chocolate drizzle, 'guilty' over the indulgent buildup. The cut at 4.33 sits on the 4.31s hit right as the clip ends; other cuts land near hits (5.03, 8.0, 10.5). No original ASMR sounds of pouring or crunching are prominent.
study.transitions: Hard cuts only. The cut at 7.8s goes into an out-of-focus frame that then racks into focus, an in-camera focus pull rather than an edit effect. The final half-second has a fast camera move to the side reveal.
study.effects: Bright, slightly lifted exposure with punchy saturation on the reds and greens, plus noticeable sharpening that makes the chocolate highlights crisp. Shallow depth of field gives a soft creamy background. There is an in-camera rack focus at 7.8-8.23s and slow handheld drifts/push-outs within shots (e.g. 3.3-4.3s, 11.6-12.1s). No freeze frames, split screens, light leaks or zoom effects added in edit.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264 at ~5.1 Mbps: clean enough for detailed sauce gloss but not 4K-crisp, with slight softness and compression in the blurry frames. Handheld but steady, macro close-ups with shallow focus. Exposure is bright and clean with a white background, so it feels like a tidy professional dessert shop rather than a home kitchen. The clear cup, consistent framing and glossy lighting make it look premium even on a phone.
study.ending: It ends on the finished product: a quick pull-back at 11.6-12.1s revealing the full layered cup through the clear plastic. It cuts almost immediately after the reveal (under 0.5s) while the camera is still moving (motion 89.6). The abrupt end flows back to the strawberry-only opening, so the loop shows the before/after.
study.why_viral: 1) It rides the Dubai chocolate trend: the item name is in the text from frame 1 and fits the 'pov: us' meme format with a recognizable trending audio. 2) Layer-by-layer reveal with escalating color contrast (red → glossy brown → neon green → gold → pistachio) gives a new satisfying payoff every 2-3 seconds. 3) Glossy macro sauce drizzles and falling crumbs are classic satisfying food footage, shot without hands so the food fills the screen. 4) The short 12s length and loop from bare strawberries to loaded cup encourage rewatches.
lessons: Name the trending item in on-screen text from frame 1 (e.g. 'pov: us whenever we make a ___'). Keep it in the upper third, white lowercase, on screen the whole video, ~10 words max.
Give one shot per layer/topping and keep the camera framing identical across shots. Each cut then reads as a clear before/after build-up.
Hold the pours: let each drizzle or sauce shot run 2-3s (here 3.07s and 2.57s). Use 0.4-0.9s shots only to bridge into the next layer.
Save the strongest color contrast for around 40-50% of the runtime (the green-on-brown drizzle at ~43%) and set it up with a few seconds of the plainer base color first.
Shoot macro, eye-level at the rim of a clear vessel, with tools entering from the top edge and no hands. Use bright soft light to create specular highlights on sauces.
Put the first cut on a strong audio hit (cut at 4.33s on the 4.31s hit). Pair the footage with a short trending voice clip whose words match the indulgence.
End with a pull-back to the full finished product, cut within ~0.5s of the reveal, and leave the opening as the 'before' state so the video loops.
Keep it under ~12-15s with roughly 5-6 cuts per 10s for assembly videos. Add light saturation and sharpening so reds and greens pop on phone screens.

study.format: New-menu launch reel / drink build montage: pour shots, overflow drips, whipped-cream topping, then a lineup reveal set to a trending song (Sabrina Carpenter 'Espresso', per the IG music tag).
study.item: Four 'frappe refreshers' from Shibam Coffee Co.: mango (deep yellow), lavender (lilac with a dark purple syrup base), green apple (neon lime) and dragonfruit (hot pink with magenta syrup base). They are served in clear branded glass mugs and finished with tall whipped-cream swirls, and the dragonfruit gets freeze-dried dragonfruit pieces. The visual hooks are the saturated candy colours, the thick frappe pouring as a ribbon into clear glass, the syrup-to-frappe layering, and the frappe deliberately overflowing and running down the outside of the glass.
study.hook: Frame 1 at 0.0s is a thick, glossy yellow ribbon of mango frappe pouring into an empty clear glass mug with the Shibam logo, shot at eye level on a white counter with blurred café shelves behind. Serif text sits in the top third: 'NOW INTRODUCING' over italic 'frappe refreshers'. The song opens on 'No, yeah' at 0.00–0.88s. By ~0.9s a yellow 'mango' label box pops in. It stops the scroll because there is constant liquid motion from frame 1, a single bold colour against a neutral background, and an immediate 'new menu item' promise.

beats.what: Mango frappe ribbon pours into an empty branded glass. 'NOW INTRODUCING frappe refreshers' title is on screen and the 'mango' label appears ~0.9s.
Mango fills the glass to the top, held at eye level until a whip blur at 2.37s.
Lavender frappe pours into a glass with a dark purple syrup base. A lilac 'lavender' label box appears, empty first and then filled with the word.
Tighter lavender angle as speckled frappe rises over the syrup, cut on the beat.
Whip-blur transition into the green apple pour, with a green 'green apple' label and a rainbow/chromatic glow on the image.
Green apple glass filled past the brim, with lime frappe starting to sheet and drip down the outside. A near-still hold at 6.0–6.5s.
Dragonfruit pours into a glass with a magenta syrup base, with the finished mango drink blurred behind. Pink 'dragonfruit' label.
Dragonfruit overflows. Thick pink rivulets run down the logo glass and pool on the counter, with a neon pink glow outline around the glass.
White light-leak flash transition into the topping sequence.
Gloved hand sprays whipped cream onto the mango in a tight close-up, then the shot ends in a whip blur.
Whipped cream swirled onto the lavender, then onto the dragonfruit, with the other drinks soft in the background.
Whipped cream piled high on the green apple in a low close-up.
Lineup of all four topped drinks on marble, slow lateral glide, with dragonfruit pieces on the pink one.
Light-leak flash, then a handheld 45° pass over pairs of drinks (mango/lavender, lavender/dragonfruit, dragonfruit/green apple).
Eye-level hero of dragonfruit and green apple. A large Shibam Coffee Co. logo overlay appears ~19.2s and holds to the end.

study.how_food_is_shown: Almost everything is eye level or slightly below, with the glass filling most of the 9:16 frame, so the logo on the glass and the colour of the liquid dominate. Pours are framed so the ribbon enters from the top edge. The pour stage happens on a white counter with warm, blurred café shelving behind. The topping and lineup stage moves to a beige textured plaster wall and white marble counter in soft natural window light. Hands appear only as a black nitrile glove holding a red-and-white whipped-cream can, which reads clean and pro and contrasts with the pastels. Clear glass shows layering (syrup base, then frappe) and texture (speckles, froth). Finished drinks are staggered in depth so one is sharp and the others are soft colour blocks. A late 45° handheld angle (16.23–18.5s) shows the swirl tops and the marble.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0.0–2.37s: mango pour, medium close, ~2.4s, ribbon visible top to bottom, smooth motion (motion 7–9). 2.37–3.07s: lavender pour into syrup, close, 0.7s. 3.07–3.8s: tighter lavender showing speckled froth rising, 0.73s. ~4.2–5.57s: green apple pour, close, ~1.4s. 5.57–7.33s: green apple overflow, very close, glass fills the frame, ~1.8s, almost static at 6.0–6.5s (motion 3.4–3.9) while drips creep down. 7.33–~8.2s: dragonfruit pour with mango behind. ~8.2–9.67s: dragonfruit overflow macro-ish, ~1.4s, thick pink drips reaching the counter and pooling. ~9.9–11.5s: whipped cream onto mango, tight on the nozzle and rosettes. 11.57–13.6s: cream onto lavender, then dragonfruit. 13.6–14.7s: cream onto green apple, low and very close, cream filling the upper frame. All play at roughly normal speed; the drips may be slightly slowed (low confidence).
study.money_shot: The dragonfruit overflow, ~8.3–9.67s (≈41–48% of the video), held ~1.4s. Thick pink frappe pours over the rim and runs in fat rivulets down the logo glass, pooling on the counter, with a pink neon glow outline. It is set up by the green apple overflow at 5.57–7.33s, which teaches the viewer the 'pour past the brim' payoff, and by the dragonfruit pour shot right before it. It is followed by a white light-leak flash at 9.67s that resets into the whipped-cream topping sequence.
study.pacing: Fast montage, with 12 shots in 20.2s (5.45 cuts/10s). Median shot is 1.77s, longest 2.37s (opening mango pour), shortest 0.7s (lavender). The structure runs in three blocks: four pours with overflows (0–9.67s, one flavour every ~2.3s), toppings (9.67–14.7s), and lineup/logo (14.7–20.2s). The song's beat hits every ~0.57s (≈104 BPM). Cuts at 3.8 (hit 3.84), 7.33 (7.3), 9.67 (9.61) and 13.6 (13.66) land on beats; others sit within ~0.25s. There are no long ASMR holds. The calmest moment is the ~1s near-still overflow at 6.0–6.5s, and median motion is 20.8, so the edit keeps moving.
study.speed: Mostly normal speed. Pours read as real-time liquid with thick viscosity. The overflow drips at 5.6–7.3s and 8.3–9.6s are slow and smooth (motion drops to 3.4–3.9 at 6.0–6.5s) and could be mild slow motion or simply viscous frappe; confidence is low. Motion spikes at 2.0s (35.8), 11.0–12.0s (40.1/47.6), 14.5s (44.4) and 18.5s (36.4) come from fast whip pans/blur transitions, not speed ramps. There are no timelapses.
study.on_screen_text: Title 0–2.37s in the top third: 'NOW INTRODUCING' in small white all-caps serif with soft drop shadow, over 'frappe refreshers' in large white italic lowercase serif. That is 4 words, removed at the first cut. Flavour labels sit lower-left/centre at ~72% height: one lowercase serif word in a rounded box colour-matched to the drink. 'mango' is black on a yellow box from ~0.9 to 2.37s. 'lavender' is dark on a lilac box from 2.37 to ~3.9s. 'green apple' is white on a bright green box from ~4.0 to 7.33s. 'dragonfruit' is white on a hot pink box from 7.33 to ~10s. Each box appears empty first, with the word filling in a few frames later (visible in the after-cut frames at 2.37 and 7.33). From ~19.2s to the end, a large full-colour Shibam Coffee Co. logo (building and cup emblem, 'Shíbam COFFEE CO.') overlays the centre. No prices.
study.audio: Trending pop track (Sabrina Carpenter 'Espresso', per the IG music tag). The only 'speech' is the song's 'No, yeah' at 0.00–0.88s. Beats hit roughly every 0.57s (2.13, 2.69, 3.28, 3.84, 4.14…19.99), and flavour changes and the topping/lineup sections are cut to them. No voiceover. Pour and spray sounds are not evident; music carries everything.
study.transitions: Hard cut at 3.07 (lavender to tighter lavender). Whip-pan/motion-blur transitions at 2.37 (mango to lavender, blurred outgoing frame), 3.8 (lavender to green apple, heavy blur in), 11.57 (mango cream to lavender cream) and 13.6 (to green apple cream). White/rainbow light-leak flashes at 9.67 (dragonfruit to whipped cream) and 16.23 (lineup to 45° pass). A soft-blur cut at 14.7 into the lineup. A hard cut at 18.53 into the final hero.
study.effects: Strong warm, high-saturation grade throughout. Rainbow chromatic-aberration/prism glow on green apple frames (~5.2–7.0s). Neon pink glow outline around the dragonfruit glass (~8.2–9.0s). Light-leak/lens-flare bursts with rainbow bokeh at 9.67s and 16.23s, plus a bloomy, washed haze on the 45° shots at 16.2–17.5s. Motion blur on the whip transitions. Logo sticker overlay at ~19.2s. Slight softening and glow on highlights overall.
study.quality: 720×1280 at 30fps, h264, ~5.6 Mbps. Exported resolution is modest and several clips look upscaled or soft, with recompression artifacts on the pours. Footage is handheld with smooth glides on the lineup. Exposure is bright and clean in window light. It reads 'café-made but polished': branded glassware, black gloves, a marble counter and colour-blocked drinks do the premium work, while the heavy filters and glows give it a trendy social look rather than a high-end commercial one.
study.ending: Ends on the finished-product lineup (dragonfruit and green apple, eye level) with the big brand logo overlay from ~19.2s, held ~1s, cutting at 20.2s mid-song. There is no bite or sip and no spoken CTA. The pastel lineup returning to a single-glass framing loops reasonably back into the opening mango pour.
study.why_viral: Four saturated, colour-coded drinks give constant visual novelty: a new colour roughly every 2s. The over-the-brim overflow drips are a satisfying 'too full' payoff that viewers want to see again. Cuts are synced to a trending song, so it feels quick and shareable. The 'now introducing' framing plus colour-matched flavour labels make it instantly readable as a menu launch that drives store visits.
lessons: Open on liquid already moving in frame 1 and put a 3–5 word 'NOW INTRODUCING [item]' title in the top third for the first ~2.4s only.
For a multi-flavour launch, give each flavour its own ~1.8–2.3s pour shot and a one-word label in a box colour-matched to the drink. Change the box colour with every flavour.
Build to a sensory payoff at ~30–50% of runtime (overflow, drip, cheese pull), and teach it once before the strongest version, like green apple at 28% then dragonfruit at 41–48%.
Shoot in clear glassware on a white or marble surface so layers (syrup base, then frappe, then cream) and colour read instantly. Keep backgrounds neutral and blurred.
Cut on the music beat. At ~104 BPM, land cuts within 0.1s of a hit at section changes, and keep the median shot under ~1.8s for a 20s reel.
Structure in three acts: pours (≈50%), topping/assembly (≈25%), lineup reveal plus logo (≈25%), with a flash or light-leak transition marking each act change.
Use whip-blur transitions between near-identical setups (same glass, different colour) so repetitive shots feel like one continuous move.
Finish on all products together staggered in depth, then lay the brand logo over the final ~1s rather than adding a separate end card.
Keep hands gloved and props simple, with one bold-coloured tool like the red cream can, so topping shots look clean and pro without distracting from the food.

study.format: Making-of / drink build (iced layered matcha latte with cold foam) cut to a trending voice/lyric sound with word-synced kinetic captions
study.item: Shibam Coffee Co. iced matcha latte. A yellow sauce is drizzled down the inside of a clear branded cup, then milk and ice go in, then whisked bright-green matcha is poured on top. A thick white cold foam is ribboned over the drink. The finished cup shows clear horizontal layers through the plastic: yellow streaks, creamy white milk, vivid green matcha and a domed white foam cap marbled with green streaks. The cup's large printed logo faces camera in every shot.
study.hook: First frame (0.0s): a close, slightly tilted shot of gloved black hands squeezing a white bottle with a red cap. Bright yellow sauce streaks down the inside of an empty clear cup. The voice says "Relax," at 0.00 with an audio hit at 0.04, and the caption "relax." pops center-frame. It stops the scroll because there is instant motion and saturated color from frame one, the black gloves contrast strongly with the yellow sauce, and the calm, oddly specific spoken line feels like a meme sound rather than an ad.

beats.what: Close-up of yellow sauce squeezed down the inside wall of the tilted branded cup. Caption: "relax."
High 45° close-up of a bamboo chasen whisking green matcha in a pink spouted bowl, gloved hands, digital scale behind. Caption: "chill." The cut lands on the word.

Wider shot: the milk/ice cup with yellow streaks sits foreground-left while whisking continues behind. Then the pink bowl tips and a green matcha stream pours in, building a green layer over the white. Captions: "breathe." then "have a Matcha", which changes font as it holds.
High-angle look into the finished green-topped cup, ice cubes poking through the matcha, layers visible. Caption: "SIT BACK".
Eye-level shot: a small pitcher pours thick white cold foam onto the green top. Caption: "it's cooler than tea".

Tighter, higher-angle shot of the cold foam falling as a slow thick ribbon onto a growing white dome with green streaks bleeding through. The pitcher lifts away and the shot ends on the foam-capped cup. Captions: "it's a little ice" then "little colder than tea".
Eye-level hero of the finished cup on the marble counter, bottle-lined bar behind. All layers and the logo face camera, with a gentle handheld drift.
Final caption payoff "but" then "Matcha" in script, over the still hero cup until the end at 9.2s.

study.how_food_is_shown: Angles mix a high 45° look-down (whisk at 0.87s, foam dome at 3.13s and 5.13s) with near eye-level side shots (pours at 1.4s and 4.2s, hero at 6.9s). Side shots show the layers through the clear cup, and the high shots show surface texture: ice, foam, marbling. Distance is medium-close: the cup fills about 40–60% of frame width, with no extreme macro. Black nitrile-gloved hands are in frame for every prep and pour shot, which reads as professional and hygienic and makes the colors pop. The background is real café context: a white-and-gold marble counter, rows of syrup squeeze bottles, a Torani bottle and a scale, shallow but not blurred. Lighting is bright, even indoor/natural light with a slight warm tone and no visible steam (iced drink). Color emphasis is the green/white/yellow stack plus a pink bowl as a complementary prop against the green. The cup is always turned so the Shibam logo faces camera.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0.0–0.87s: yellow sauce squeezed down the cup wall, close, normal speed, held 0.87s. 0.87–1.4s: whisk churning green matcha, close high angle, 0.53s and the highest motion of the video (motion 26–31 around 0.5–1.5s). About 1.9–3.13s: green matcha stream from the pink bowl's spout into the cup, medium-close eye level, about 1.2s of the 1.73s shot, normal speed, showing the green layer settling over the white milk. 4.2–5.13s: cold foam pour from a pitcher onto the green top, medium eye level, 0.93s. 5.13–about 6.6s: the cold foam ribbon thickening into a dome with green streaks, closer and higher, about 1.5s within a 1.77s shot. It plays smooth and syrupy, but motion stays 10–20, consistent with normal-speed thick foam rather than obvious slow motion. No cut-open or sipping shots.
study.money_shot: The cold foam ribbon pour at 5.13–6.9s, about 56–75% of the video. A thick, glossy white stream folds onto the drink and builds a domed cap while green matcha streaks marble through it. It's held about 1.77s, the second-longest shot. Setup: the matcha layer pour (1.4–3.13s) and the bare green-top reveal (3.13s) show the drink without foam first, so the foam reads as the finishing transformation. The first foam angle (4.2s) teases it before the closer angle pays it off. It's followed directly by the 2.3s eye-level hero of the finished layered cup.
study.pacing: Fast and rhythmic up front, settling into holds at the end. Shots run 0.87, 0.53, 1.73, 1.07, 0.93, 1.77 and 2.3s, with a median of 1.07s and 6.52 cuts per 10s. The two quickest shots (0.87s, 0.53s) carry the first two one-word lines, "relax" and "chill". Pours get longer holds (1.73s, 1.77s) and the hero gets the longest (2.3s). Cuts lock to the voice: 0.87s on "chill" (0.88) and an audio hit (0.9), 1.4s on "breathe" (1.40), 4.2s on "it's" (4.24) and hit (4.27), 6.9s on "tea" (6.96) and hit (7.0). The 3.13s cut lands just before "sit" (3.26). Motion falls from 31 near the start to 4.9–5.5 in the final second, so the video literally calms down as the voice says relax and sit back.
study.speed: Essentially none. Everything appears to play at normal speed. The foam pour (5.13–6.9s) looks languid, but motion values (10–17) and the natural fall of thick cold foam suggest real-time, with at most a very mild slowdown (low confidence). No speed ramps or timelapses are detected.
study.on_screen_text: None beyond the speech captions. The only other text is the printed "Shibam Coffee Co. Organic · Yemeni · Premium" branding on the cup itself, which functions as built-in product naming. No prices or item-name graphics.
study.captions:
Present throughout, word/phrase-synced to the voice and placed dead center over the cup (about the middle third of the frame). The style is white text with a black outline/shadow, and the font changes almost every phrase as a kinetic effect:
- lowercase rounded bold for "relax.", "chill." and "breathe."
- a small "have a" over a large bold serif "Matcha" that switches to a distressed font, then italic script while held
- caps bold "SIT BACK"
- bold "it's cooler than tea"
- a cursive-ish "it's a little ice"
- "little colder than tea" cycling through lowercase, then italic distressed caps, then a smaller script, then plain
- the final "but" and script "Matcha"
Captions show 1–4 words at a time, changing exactly on the word timestamps.
study.audio: A trending spoken/sung voice sound ("Relax, chill, breathe, have a matcha, sit back, it's cooler than tea… but matcha"), 23 words starting at 0.00s and running the full 9.18s. It acts as both hook and soundtrack. There is no audible ASMR pour or whisk sound emphasized. Strong audio hits at 0.04, 0.68, 0.9, 2.63, 3.3, 3.61, 4.27, 4.96, 5.79, 6.44, 7.0, 7.78 and 9.04. Several align with cuts (0.9, 4.27, 7.0) and with the final word "matcha" (7.98) landing on the static hero.
study.transitions: Hard cuts only, at 0.87, 1.4, 3.13, 4.2, 5.13 and 6.9. The cut pairs show continuity of action: the whisk continues across 1.4s, and the foam pour continues across 5.13s from a closer angle, giving a smooth cut-on-action feel rather than any effect.
study.effects: Minimal. There is slight handheld drift and a gentle push/rise in the foam shot (5.13–6.9s) and the hero shot (6.9–9.2s), plus a mildly warm, bright, slightly saturated look. No freeze frames, split screens, flashes or zoom effects. The animated font-swapping captions are the main stylistic effect.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264, about 4660 kbps. The footage is clean but slightly soft, typical of a phone re-encoded for social. It's handheld with small drifts, well exposed with bright even light and no blown highlights on the white foam, and low noise. It looks professional-casual: a real café bar (marble, syrup bottles, gloved barista, branded cup) rather than a studio. That authenticity, plus the clean layer separation in the clear cup, makes it feel premium but attainable.
study.ending: Ends on the finished drink. A 2.3s eye-level hero of the layered cup holds while the voice delivers "but… matcha" (7.80–7.98s) and the caption "Matcha" sits over the logo. Motion drops to about 5, so it's nearly still, and the video ends at 9.2s, about 1.2s after the last word. It loops cleanly, since the calm hero flows back into the punchy "relax" squeeze at 0s.
study.why_viral: 1) A memeable trending voice line, word-synced with playful font-switching captions, makes it feel like entertainment, not an ad, and invites rewatching to catch the words. 2) Strong color layering (yellow, white, green, foam) visible through a clear cup builds in clear steps, so viewers stay to see the final stack. 3) Satisfying pours, especially the thick cold foam ribbon marbling with green, give the payoff at about 60–75%. 4) The video is under 10 seconds with cuts on every word and a still, looping ending, which drives completion and replays.
lessons: Open on motion and saturated color in frame one: a squeeze, drizzle or pour in the first 0.5s, never an empty setup shot.
Cut on the words of the voiceover or sound. Here 4 of 6 cuts land within 0.06s of a spoken word or audio hit. Snap each cut to the nearest word or beat.
Keep prep shots short (0.5–1s) and give pours 1.5–1.8s and the final hero 2–2.5s, so the edit decelerates toward the payoff.
Show a drink's layers from eye level through a clear cup and texture from a high 45° angle. Alternate the two so viewers get both the stack and the surface.
Build in order of visual change: base, then color layer, then a reveal without topping, then topping pour, then hero. Show the before so the final topping reads as a transformation.
Cover the same key pour from two angles (wide, then tighter) and hard-cut on the action so the motion continues across the cut.
Use word-synced center captions of 1–4 words, white with a dark stroke, over the product. Swapping fonts on emphasis words (like the product name) adds energy without extra graphics.
Turn the branded cup or packaging to face camera in every shot. It does the item-naming work, so no price or title overlay is needed.
End on a near-still hero (motion dropping to about 5) for 1–2s after the last word so the video loops smoothly back into the high-energy first shot.
Keep total length under about 10s for a single-item build. That leaves room for roughly 6–7 shots without any shot outstaying its welcome.

study.format: Restaurant menu montage / food b-roll reel: kitchen process shots (grilling, saucing, scooping, tossing) intercut with finished-dish macro hero shots, set to music with no voiceover.
study.item: A Middle Eastern shawarma shop's menu. It shows mixed-grill platters (charred beef kebab, kofta, paprika chicken, blistered red, yellow and orange peppers, translucent grilled onion on yellow turmeric rice), chicken and beef shawarma wraps with white garlic sauce and pickles, wraps toasted on a griddle with a glistening sauce-filled cross-section, hummus with chickpeas and green herb sauce, seasoned fries, and the salad, pickle and olive bar. What makes it visual is the color contrast (saturated yellow rice, red and orange peppers, white sauce against dark char), the grill marks, and the shiny, saucy textures.
study.hook: Frame one is a tight, low, near-grill-level shot of kofta, a beef patty and chicken on a grate with large orange flames licking up behind them and smoke drifting. It opens on music only, with no text or speech. Motion jumps from 25.9 to 59.6 by 1.0s as the fire moves, and within about 2s it switches to a spoon spreading hummus over bright yellow rice. Live fire plus char marks is an instant 'this is real grilled meat' signal, and the bright orange fills the frame before a viewer can scroll.

beats.what: Flames roaring over kofta, patty and chicken on the grill
Hummus spread in a takeout container next to yellow rice, finished with parsley and chickpeas (gloved hand)
Macro slide across a finished mixed-grill platter: beef kebab, kofta, chicken, peppers
Wrap loaded with garlic sauce and pickles, then sliced wrap halves with a blade, then a seasoned fries close-up
Yellow rice scooped into a container, then a rack-focus row of sliced chicken shawarma wraps (jump cut at 12.0)
Slow pan down a packed platter in a container, then a tighter macro of the char
Hummus and salad in the box, then gloved hands laying pickles beside chicken shawarma on bread
Garlic sauce drizzled in streams over chicken shawarma with pickles
Beef shawarma piled on bread, tomatoes and onions added
Grill with smoke and tongs turning meat, then green herb sauce spooned onto hummus and chickpeas
Glossy peppers and onion on the grill grates
Cut wrap in a combo box with pickled turnips and a garlic sauce cup
Platter shot outdoors with a light flare, then in front of the steam table
Fries tossed with seasoning in a steel bowl
Rack focus from blur to sharp on a toasted wrap end on the griddle, sauce and paprika oozing out
Tongs working kebab, kofta and peppers on the grill
Lettuce in the bar, rice in a box, chopped salad spooned in
Beef shawarma with garlic sauce and tomatoes, rainbow light leak
Platter macro, griddled wrap end reprised, more platter macros
Grill veg and kofta, then fries tossed
Fries handled, then a tour of the bar: olives, pickles, parsley, chili sauce
Final still hold on the glistening griddled wrap cross-section

study.how_food_is_shown: Almost everything is macro or very close (food fills 70-100% of the 9:16 frame), shot at eye level or a low 15-30° angle so the food towers in the frame. Depth of field is very shallow: the background (steel kitchen, steam table, griddle backsplash) melts into blur and rack focus is used repeatedly. There are some 45° overhead-ish shots of containers and the steam-table bins. Hands appear only as black nitrile gloves holding tongs, spoons or a squeeze bottle; black gloves and black takeout trays act as a dark frame that makes the yellow rice, red peppers and white sauce pop. Lighting is bright, mostly daylight-white kitchen light with specular highlights on oil, sauce and grill marks. One outdoor platter shot uses natural light and a greenery background. Flames and smoke are visible in the grill shots. Color is pushed hard toward yellow, orange and red, and textures are emphasized: char lines, crispy fry edges, glossy sauce.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0-1.5s: flames over meat at close range, normal speed. 1.5-3.47s: spoon swirling hummus, macro. 3.47-5.6s: macro slide over kebab and chicken char, about 2s. 6.38s: knife blade over sliced wrap halves, close. 7.79-8.8s: fries macro with a shallow focal plane. 9.21s: rice tumbling from a scoop, motion-blurred. 10.62-13.57s: rack-focus row of wrap cross-sections, about 3s. 14.88s: extreme macro of kofta and chicken char. 17.4-19.87s (about 2.5s): garlic sauce drizzle, with streams visible falling from the bottle at 19.12s; possibly mildly slowed. 20.54-22.5s: beef shawarma macro. 24.79s: smoke and tongs through haze. 26.21s: green sauce spooned onto hummus, a thick dollop at close range. 27.0-29s: glistening peppers on the grates. 30.46-33.1s: wrap cut-open with exposed meat. 36.12-38.4s: fries tossed in a bowl, fast with motion blur. 38.4-40.4s (about 2s): wrap end on the griddle rack-focusing from blur to sharp, showing sauce oozing and paprika. 51.71s: same wrap cross-section reprised. 53.12s: kebab macro with parsley. 57.38s: fries lifted with tongs. 64.67-68s (about 3.3s): final hold on the sauce-filled wrap end.
study.money_shot: The griddled wrap cross-section: a toasted, char-spotted wrap standing on a black griddle with a glossy, sauce-soaked filling and a paprika-dusted edge. It first lands at 38.4-40.4s (about 56-59% of the video), set up by the fast, blurry fry-toss shot at 35.63s and then revealed through a rack focus from full blur to sharp over about 1.5s. It is followed by busy grill action at 40.4s. It is reprised at 51.7s and becomes the final shot from 64.67s to the end, about 3.3s with motion falling to 8-10, so the most appetizing frame is the one the video ends on.
study.pacing: Fast, steady montage: 25 shots in 68s (3.53 cuts per 10s), median shot 2.7s, range 1.57-4.43s. Several detected shots actually contain two or three subjects through quick camera moves or soft cuts (0-3.47, 5.6-8.8, 22.57-27.0), so the felt rhythm is closer to one image every 1.5-2s. Median motion is 35.1 and stays high throughout, with repeated spikes of 70-89 from tongs, tossing and whip-like moves (around 17.5, 32, 35.5, 45, 48.5, 61.5s). Process shots (high motion) alternate with finished-dish macro slides (motion 15-30). No audio hits were detected, so cuts don't appear to be precisely beat-matched. The edit ends on a deliberate still hold, with motion dropping to 8-10 at 65-67.5s.
study.speed: Mostly real-time. Fry tossing (36s, 57s), rice scooping (9s) and the grill tongs show natural motion blur, so they are not slowed. The garlic sauce drizzle at 17.4-19.9s and the smooth macro slides over the platters look gently slowed or shot at high frame rate (low, even motion of 15-30), but I'm not confident. There are no clear speed ramps or timelapses.
study.on_screen_text: none
study.audio: A licensed music track runs under the whole video. There is no voiceover and no speech; the transcript is empty. No strong audio transients were detected, so there is no ASMR emphasis (no isolated sizzle or crunch hits) and no sound effects on cuts. The music alone carries the energy, and picture-to-sound sync is loose rather than cut-on-beat.
study.transitions: Mostly hard cuts. Cuts at 12.0, 13.57 and 27.0 join nearly identical framings, so they act as jump cuts or retakes. Several in-shot camera whips and focus blurs work as transitions: around 1.5s (fire to hummus), 6-7.5s (wrap to blade to fries), 29.04s (full defocus), 36.12s (whip blur on the fry toss), 44.62s and 63.04s (motion blur sweeps), and 38.96s (rack focus from blur into the money shot). There are no flashes, zooms or graphic wipes.
study.effects: Heavy saturation and warmth, with yellows and oranges especially boosted on the rice, peppers and fries. Strong sharpening and clarity on the char textures, plus high contrast. Light leaks or lens flares appear over the platter at 33.29s and as a rainbow flare at 47.46s. There are repeated rack focuses and very shallow depth of field. Handheld and gimbal slides and push-ins run along the food. There are no freeze frames or split screens.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264 at about 6.1 Mbps, which is good bitrate for 720p, so the macros stay crisp. Footage is mostly gimbal-smooth slides with some handheld shake and motion blur in the action shots. Exposure is bright and clean with no muddy shadows; there is some oversharpening halo and oversaturation that reads as 'Instagram commercial'. Tight macros, shallow focus and a deliberate grade push it above typical homemade footage, while the black takeout containers and steam-table shots keep it authentic and fast-casual.
study.ending: It ends on the finished hero item: a 3.3s near-static hold (64.67-68s, motion 8-10) of the glistening griddled wrap cross-section with no CTA or text. The shot it ends on also appeared at 38.4s and 51.7s, so the loop back to the flaming grill opener feels natural.
study.why_viral: 1) An open-flame opener: fire and char on meat in the first second is a primal scroll-stopper. 2) Relentless macro texture and color, with grill marks, white garlic sauce over meat, saturated yellow rice and blistered peppers, all filling the frame so every 2s brings a new craving cue. 3) A behind-the-counter process (saucing, scooping, tossing, grilling) intercut with finished boxes, so it reads as both 'look how it's made' and 'here's exactly what you get'. 4) The repeated, rack-focused sauce-filled wrap cross-section gives a signature money shot that it returns to and ends on.
lessons: Open on the most primal visual you have (flames, smoke, sizzle) at close range in frame 1; no title card and no text.
Shoot food at 15-30° or eye level, not overhead, and fill 70-100% of the vertical frame so it looks huge.
Keep shots 1.5-3s (median about 2.7s) for a menu montage, and alternate a high-motion process shot (toss, scoop, tongs) with a slow macro slide over a finished dish.
Use a rack focus from full blur to sharp (about 1.5s) to reveal your hero item; it builds a mini-anticipation moment without any effects.
Pick one signature money shot (cross-section, sauce pull, cut-open) and show it 2-3 times: around the midpoint, around 75%, and as a 3s+ still hold at the end.
Put bright food in black containers and black gloves; the dark surround makes yellows, reds and white sauces pop after a saturation boost.
Grade warm and saturated, with extra clarity on char and crust, but watch for sharpening halos at 720p.
Use camera whips and focus blurs as free transitions between subjects instead of graphic effects.
If there's no voiceover, let music carry the energy and spend every second on food; skip faces, prices and filler shots.

study.format: Making-of / process promo for a restaurant opening. It is a griddle-to-sandwich build with no voice and only music and ambience, ending on a branded 'coming soon' address card.
study.item: A Philly-style cheesesteak from Omars Seafood & Grill. Visual appeal comes from: bright red and green bell pepper strips and onions; thin shaved ribeye that goes from raw pink to seared brown; seasoning dust; heavy steam off a black flat-top; a blanket of melted white cheese bubbling in the grease; and a final orange-pink cheese sauce glistening over the meat on a toasted roll. The colors are saturated red and green against dark steel, then glossy beige and orange against a clean white background at the end.
study.hook: The first frame (0-0.67s) is an eye-level macro shot sitting right on the griddle surface. Glossy red pepper strips fill the bottom two-thirds, and a black-gloved hand drops green pepper strips that are caught mid-air with motion blur. There is no text and no voice; it opens on music. It stops the scroll because of the extreme low, close angle, the high-contrast red and green on a black surface, and immediate physical motion (food falling toward the lens). At 0.67s it cuts to the same veg already sizzling, so the viewer is in 'cooking' within one second.

beats.what: Macro, griddle-level: gloved hand drops red and green pepper strips onto the flat-top.
Peppers and onions sizzling, shot low across the griddle with shallow focus.
Shaved steak, raw pink to browning, is chopped into the veg with a metal spatula.
Seasoning dust falls through the frame onto the meat-and-pepper pile, held for 1.77s.
Long 3.23s low macro of steam rolling off the seasoned steak, with grease bubbling in the foreground.
Spatula tosses saucy, glossy steak with red peppers while steam rises.
Second spatula chop and toss.
Spatula folds the mix; sauce drips off the blade.
Melted white cheese draped over the steak pile, bubbling in the grease. A steam cloud washes across around 13s, landing on the 13.27 audio hit. Held for 4.97s.
Spatula slides the cheesy steak onto an open toasted roll, in macro.
Open-faced loaded roll on foil, macro eye level, slow drift across glistening cheese sauce, peppers and steak. Held for 3.5s.
Finished open sandwich on a white plate at 45°, slow push-in, 3.4s.
Closed cheesesteak in side profile on a white seamless background with the overlay: COMING SOON / Omars Seafood & Grill / 26751 BROOKPARK RD EXT, NORTH OLMSTED, OH. Held for 5.07s to the end.

study.how_food_is_shown: Nearly everything from 0-16.4s is shot at griddle level: the camera sits on or just above the flat-top at about 0-10°. Depth of field is very shallow, so the foreground and background melt into blur and steam reads as soft haze. Hands appear only in the first shot (black nitrile gloves). After that the only tools are the metal spatula blades, which also reflect light. Lighting is warm and directional from above and behind, which makes steam and seasoning particles glow and keeps the dark griddle near-black for contrast. The plating section switches backgrounds to show the 'finished product' state: crinkled foil at 18.4s, then a bright white plate and white seamless backdrop at 21.9-30.4s. Here the camera rises to about 45° for the plate and goes back to eye level for the closed-sandwich hero. Color emphasis is on red pepper, green pepper, seared brown edges and glossy cheese sauce. Texture emphasis is on steam, bubbling fat, sauce sheen and toasted bread grain.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0-0.67s: falling peppers in extreme macro at normal or slightly slowed speed, showing motion-blurred strips. 0.67-1.83s: sizzling veg macro. 1.58s: raw pink steak under the spatula edge. 2.6-4.37s: seasoning sprinkle; particles drift slowly and visibly through the frame (likely slowed), held 1.77s. 4.37-7.6s: steam macro across a 3.23s span, joined by a near-invisible jump cut at 4.37. Motion here is 4-7/100, the quietest stretch, so the steam rolls slowly and grease bubbles at the bottom edge. 7.6-11.4s: three spatula toss and chop close-ups (1.07s, 0.9s, 1.83s) with sauce dripping off the blade at 8.55s and 10.45s. 11.4-16.37s: melted cheese blanket in macro at griddle level for 4.97s. Fat bubbles at the edge (13.6-15.5s) and a steam bloom washes the frame white around 12.98s and again at 16.15s. 16.37-18.43s: macro of the steak sliding onto the roll with the spatula. 18.43-21.93s: macro drift over the sauced open roll showing cheese-sauce gloss. 21.93-25.33s: 45° plate push-in. 25.33-30.4s: side-profile cross-section of the closed sandwich. There is no cut-open, bite or cheese pull.
study.money_shot: The open-faced loaded roll on foil at 18.43-21.93s, starting at about 61% of the video and held for 3.5s. It is a macro, eye-level slow drift across glossy orange-pink cheese sauce pooling over seared steak and red and green peppers, on toasted bread. It is set up by about 16s of raw-to-cooked griddle process (seasoning, steam, cheese melt) and the spatula transfer at 16.37s, so the viewer has 'watched it being made' before seeing it finished. It is followed by a wider 45° plate view (21.93s) and then the closed-sandwich hero with the branding CTA (25.33s).
study.pacing: The video mixes fast bursts with long ASMR-style holds: 13 shots in 30.4s, 3.95 cuts per 10s, median shot 1.83s. The opening burst covers 0-2.6s with three shots of 0.67s, 1.17s and 0.77s. It then slows into holds of 1.77s (seasoning) and 3.23s (steam, the lowest motion at 4-7). A second fast burst runs 7.6-11.4s with spatula action (1.07s, 0.9s, 1.83s; motion 15-23). The longest cooking hold follows at 4.97s on the cheese melt. Finishing shots lengthen to 2.07s, 3.5s, 3.4s and 5.07s as the food becomes the finished product. The rhythm alternates energy (chopping) with calm (steam and cheese). The first audio hit at 2.0s sits inside the steak-chop shot, close to the 1.83s cut. The second at 13.27s falls inside the cheese hold, near the steam wash and the 24.9 motion spike at about 13s, rather than on a cut.
study.speed: Likely slow motion on the seasoning shot (2.6-4.37s): particles hang and drift and motion is about 8. It is also likely on the steam shot (4.37-7.6s), where motion of 4.2-6.8 gives a smooth, slow-rolling steam look. I'm moderately confident about both; they read as about 50% speed or slower rather than true high-speed. The cheese-melt shot (11.4-16.37s) also looks gently slowed, with slow bubbling and steam. The spatula tosses (7.6-11.4s) and the opening drop look like normal speed. The final shots (18.4-30.4s) are smooth slow camera drifts at steady motion of about 11-14, likely gimbal or slider moves, not speed effects. There are no timelapses and no clear in-shot speed ramps. The 33.4 spike at the final sample is likely the end or loop point.
study.on_screen_text:
Only at the end, from 25.33s to 30.4s (5.07s), in the upper third over the white backdrop above the sandwich. Four stacked elements, about 12 words at once:
- 'COMING SOON': heavy black condensed all-caps with a red outline and glow.
- 'Omars': large red script with a thick black outline and soft red glow.
- 'Seafood & Grill': smaller red script with black outline.
- '26751 BROOKPARK RD EXT' and 'NORTH OLMSTED, OH': black bold condensed all-caps with red stroke and glow.
The card appears to animate in: it fades from pinkish at the cut frame, and the address briefly glitches ('RD FXT') before settling by about 26.9s. There is no other text, prices or item names.
study.audio: No voiceover and no speech; it is driven by a music track. The strongest hits are at 2.0s, during the steak chop just after the 1.83s cut, and 13.27s, during the cheese-melt hold, coinciding with the steam bloom and motion spike. Griddle sizzle and spatula scraping ambience are probably layered under the music, since the visuals are built around sizzle, steam and chopping, but this can't be confirmed from the data. There are no obvious added sound effects.
study.transitions: Hard cuts throughout. Several are near-invisible jump cuts within the same setup: at 4.37s (steam shot continues), 9.57s (spatula fold continues), 11.4s (cheese shot continues) and 18.43s (the same spatula frame before and after, then moving to the plated roll). The cut at 16.37s comes out of a frame washed nearly white by steam, which behaves like a natural 'steam wipe' or flash into the assembly shot. The cut at 25.33s goes to the CTA hero with the text card fading or animating in. There are no whips, zooms or object wipes.
study.effects: Warm, high-saturation grade with lifted reds, oranges and greens. There is a soft bloom or glow on highlights, plus visible sharpening and clarity, which gets crunchy on the spatula shots (7.9-11s). The shallow-focus blur appears to be optical. Steam washes at about 13s and 16.15s lighten the frame almost to white. The final shots use slow push-ins and drifts (18.4-30.4s). The end card has a red outer glow on the text and a brief glitch or typing animation on the address. There are no split screens, freeze frames or light leaks.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264, about 5.9 Mbps. That is decent but not 1080p, and the heavy sharpening shows some edge haloing and compression in the steam-heavy and fast spatula shots. Most shots are stable, suggesting a tripod, slider or gimbal at griddle level. Exposure is controlled, with a dark griddle and bright steam highlights. The high-end look comes from macro lenses, very shallow depth of field, backlit steam and the clean white seamless product shots at the end. Together these read as a hired food videographer rather than phone footage, even with the 720p delivery.
study.ending: It ends on the finished closed cheesesteak in side profile with the COMING SOON / brand / address card, held for 5.07s. This is the longest shot of the video, so the address is readable. There is no bite or reaction. The final motion spike at about 30s suggests it cuts straight back to the loop start, and the falling peppers re-hook on replay.
study.why_viral: 1) Griddle-level macro with shallow focus turns a basic cheesesteak cook into cinema: steam, seasoning dust and bubbling fat glow against black steel. 2) A clear raw-to-finished transformation in 25s (pink steak → seared → cheese melt → sauced roll) delivers satisfying process payoff. 3) Rhythm contrast: fast 0.7-1.2s chop bursts are broken up by 3-5s slow holds on steam and melting cheese, which keeps attention while letting appetite build. 4) A local 'coming soon' plus exact address turns the hunger into a concrete plan to visit.
lessons: Open with motion at the food's level: put the camera on the cooking surface and have ingredients fall toward the lens in the first 0.7s, before any text.
Cut the first 2.5s fast (3 shots under 1.2s each) to establish the cook, then drop into a 3-5s slow hold on steam or melt once the viewer is invested.
Alternate energy and calm: spatula, chop or toss bursts at about 1s per shot, then a single 3-5s low-motion hold. Repeat this pattern rather than keeping one tempo.
Backlight steam and seasoning against a dark surface, and slow those shots (about 50%) so particles and steam visibly drift. They read as 'hot and fresh' instantly.
Show the full raw-to-finished transformation, and land the finished 'money shot' at about 60% of runtime, held 3-4s with a slow push-in, not at the very end.
Switch to a clean, bright background (white plate or seamless) for the finished product so it pops after the dark cooking shots.
Hold the final branded shot for 5s with no more than 4 lines of text in the top third, leaving the food unobstructed in the lower two-thirds.
For openings or local promos, put the 'COMING SOON' or offer line plus the exact address on the hero shot; no voiceover is needed if the food carries it.
Use a warm, saturated grade with mild highlight glow, but keep sharpening moderate: over-sharpened steam and metal look crunchy at 720p.

study.format: Making-of / assembly process (kitchen build of a loaded fries box), no voiceover, set to music
study.item: Loaded shrimp fries from Fatima's Grill Cleveland, served in a red-and-white branded 'FOOD FUSION' takeout box. It's built in layers: fries, shredded white cheese, creamy pink-flecked coleslaw with purple cabbage, glossy blackened shrimp in orange garlic butter, then a heavy snow of more shredded cheese. What makes it visual is the contrast between the glossy, charred orange-brown shrimp and the pale cheese and creamy slaw, plus the dripping pan butter.
study.hook: The first frame (0–0.3s) is an extreme close-up of shrimp sizzling in bubbling orange garlic-seasoned butter in a steel pan. A spoon/tong stirs them, and the blue gas flame is visible at the bottom edge. There is no text and no speech, only the music starting. Motion is high from frame one (28.3, then 26.4). It stops the scroll because there's no setup: you are dropped into hot food actively cooking, filling the frame with glistening, saturated orange.

beats.what: Macro of shrimp tossed in sizzling orange garlic butter in a steel pan over a gas flame
Blue-gloved hand spreads shredded cheese over fries in the branded box
Gloved hand piles creamy coleslaw on top of the cheese and fries; long 3.4s macro with shallow focus
Pan tilts and a spoon pushes glossy blackened shrimp off the pan onto the slaw, with butter drips falling (lands on the 8.22 beat)
Second angle of shrimp sliding off the pan with sauce pooling
Fast, heavily motion-blurred gloved hand spreading shrimp (1.0s energy shot)
Low angle across the box rim: shrimp on slaw, with 'FOOD FUSION' printing in the foreground
Glove nudges shrimp into place
Hands arrange shrimp, then pull out to a 2s hold on the full shrimp-over-slaw-and-fries layer with sauce drizzle visible
Shredded cheese rains down onto the shrimp, shreds drifting through the air
Quick 0.53s shot of the gloved hand releasing a fistful of cheese
Cheese continues falling onto the shrimp
0.4s flash of the hand dropping more cheese
Final 3.33s shot: last cheese shreds float down onto the fully loaded box; video ends on the near-still finished item

study.how_food_is_shown: Almost everything is macro or close, at roughly 30–45° or eye level. The camera sits just above the box rim, so the food fills 70–90% of the frame. There are no wide shots of the kitchen or staff faces. Blue nitrile gloves are the only 'person' in frame, and their saturated blue contrasts with the orange shrimp. Depth of field is very shallow (foreground box edge and background blurred), giving a premium, cinematic look. Lighting is warm indoor key light from above/side, so the shrimp glaze and butter catch specular highlights. Backgrounds are neutral: the white inside of the box and the dark stove. The red-printed box branding is deliberately kept in the lower foreground in shots at 2.67, 11.47 and 13.03. The emphasis is on texture: char on the shrimp, wet glossy butter, stringy shredded cheese, creamy slaw.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0–2.67s: macro stir of shrimp in bubbling butter, 2.67s, normal speed. 4.67–8.07s: tight macro of coleslaw clumps being pressed onto cheese (3.4s, longest shot), with focus falling off quickly. 8.07–9.6s: pour/slide of shrimp off the tilted pan, with orange butter strands dripping onto the slaw below. It is held 1.53s and looks slightly slowed (smooth drips, motion around 22–28). 9.6–10.47s: second slide angle, 0.87s, with sauce pooling in the pan. 11.47–13.03s: low-angle close-up across the rim, slow drift. 14.4–16.47s: near-static hold on glossy shrimp (motion drops to ~9–12), the clearest 'look at the texture' moment. 16.47–24.5s: cheese-shred rain in several shots. The shreds visibly hang and tumble through the air, which reads as slow motion. The final 3.33s shot lets the last shreds settle.
study.money_shot: The shrimp sliding off the pan onto the slaw with butter dripping, at 8.07s (33% in). It is held about 2.4s across two angles (8.07–10.47). It is set up by 5.4s of building the base (cheese, then slaw) with the shrimp only seen cooking in the hook, so the payoff is the shrimp finally landing in the box. The cut into it lands on the music hit at 8.22. It's followed immediately by a blurry 1s energy shot and then the low-angle reveal of the shrimp layer. The secondary payoff is the cheese 'snow' finale (16.47–24.5, 67–100%).
study.pacing: This is a mix: medium holds for texture, quick cuts for energy. Median shot length is 1.55s, at 5.31 cuts per 10s. The longest holds are 3.4s (slaw macro), 3.33s (final cheese) and 2.67/2.6/2.57s (hook, shrimp hold, first cheese rain). Very short punctuation shots are 0.87, 0.87, 0.53 and 0.4s, clustered around the action moments (10.47, 13.03, 19.07, 20.77). Audio hits come every ~0.255s (an ~118 BPM eighth-note grid, e.g. 7.21/7.46/7.72). Several cuts sit on or within ~0.1s of hits: 8.07→8.22, 10.47→10.51, 13.03→13.06, 19.07→19.16, 20.77→20.68. Overall rhythm: an energetic start, a fast middle section (8–14s, six cuts in 6s), then a slower, floaty cheese finale with long holds.
study.speed: Likely real slow motion on the cheese-rain shots (16.47–24.5s): shreds hang and drift visibly mid-air while motion stays low (around 7–17). Moderately confident. The shrimp slide and drips at 8.07–10.47 also look gently slowed, but this is less certain. The 10.47–11.47 shot is extremely motion-blurred and may be sped up or a fast ramp. Low confidence. No timelapses.
study.on_screen_text: none (the only text is the platform watermark/music tag, plus the 'FOOD FUSION' printing physically on the box)
study.audio: No voiceover or speech (0 words). The track is upbeat indie-pop: the platform music tag reads Capital Cities 'Safe and Sound', and the hits on a ~0.25s grid fit its ~118 BPM. No audible ASMR sizzle or crunch is indicated, so the music carries everything. Picture is synced loosely to the beat, with key action cuts (shrimp slide 8.07, cheese hand 19.07/20.77) landing near hits. The cheese finale runs over a dense cluster of hits (22.72, 22.97, 23.23, 23.74).
study.transitions: Hard cuts only. The 10.47 cut goes into a heavily motion-blurred frame that works like a whip/motion-blur transition, but it's a hard cut onto fast camera/hand movement. Several cuts are close match-ish continuations of the same action from a new angle (8.07→9.6 pan slide, 19.07→19.6→20.77→21.17 cheese drops).
study.effects: Warm, saturated grade that pushes orange/red on the shrimp and boosts contrast. Noticeable sharpening, with crunchy edges on the cheese shreds and shrimp char. Very shallow depth of field, used as a look. Slight handheld drifts and push-ins rather than added digital zooms. No freeze frames, split screens, light leaks or flashes.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264, ~5.5 Mbps: a compressed, upload-quality export, but the source clearly came from a camera with a fast or macro lens, given the strong background blur. Handheld but smooth. Exposure is well controlled, with highlights on the butter and glaze not clipped. Some softness and noise in darker frames. What reads as high-end is the shallow focus, tight macro framing, warm grade and clean branded packaging. Homemade touches are the motion-blurred shot and a few soft-focus frames.
study.ending: Ends on the finished item: the final 3.33s shot (21.17–24.5) of the last cheese shreds falling onto the shrimp-topped box, with motion settling to ~7 before the cut. There is no bite, reaction or CTA. It cuts off while the cheese is still settling, so it loops reasonably well back into the sizzling pan.
study.why_viral: 1) Instant sizzle hook: glistening orange butter shrimp in macro from frame one, with no intro. 2) Layer-by-layer build creates anticipation, paid off when glossy shrimp slide off the pan with dripping butter on the beat. 3) Extreme abundance: fistfuls of cheese and heaps of slaw and shrimp, ending in a slow cheese 'snowfall' that feels indulgent. 4) Upbeat recognizable track and beat-matched cuts keep 24.5s moving, while shallow-focus macros make takeout food look premium.
lessons: Open on the hottest, glossiest moment (sizzle, bubbling sauce) in macro, filling 80%+ of the frame, with no text or intro in the first 2s.
Build the item in layers and save the hero ingredient's transfer (pan to plate/box) for about 30–35% into the video. Hold it 1.5–2.5s across two angles.
Cut on music hits: snap key action cuts to within ~0.1s of a beat. For a ~118 BPM track that means cut points every ~0.5s.
Mix pacing: 2.5–3.5s texture holds for macros and finales, 0.4–0.9s punch shots around action moments. Aim for a ~1.5s median and ~5 cuts per 10s.
Shoot sprinkles, drips and drops (cheese, sauce, herbs) at 60fps+ and play them slowed. Give the final topping 'snowfall' 3s+ as the closer.
Keep branded packaging in the foreground of 2–3 shots (low angle across the rim) so the business is identified without overlay text.
Use a warm grade with boosted orange/red saturation and moderate sharpening on cooked proteins. Contrasting glove or prop colors (blue vs orange) help the food pop.
Use shallow depth of field and get the lens 10–20cm from the food: blurred foregrounds and backgrounds make simple takeout look premium.
End on the finished item mid-motion, not a static plate. Cutting while the final ingredient is still settling makes the loop back to the opening sizzle feel seamless.

study.format: Making-of / process drink build, shot ASMR-style with no voice: a smoothie-shop order made from start to finish behind the counter.
study.item: Strawberry banana smoothie at Blendz. It is built from water and soft-serve mix, frost-covered frozen strawberries, frozen banana slices and a scoop of golden powder, then blended in a Vitamix. The visual payoff is the cup: whipped cream is smeared up the inside walls with a twisted bar spoon, and thick hot-pink smoothie is poured in. The result is bold pink-and-white candy-cane spirals around the branded cup. Frosty fruit textures and the saturated pink against white cream are the visual hooks.
study.hook: First frame (0-1.67s): a gloved hand pumps water from a white dispenser into an empty blender jar, filmed from a close eye-level angle. A bold white title, 'Strawberry Banana Smoothie', sits mid-upper frame with '✨asmr edition✨' under it. The first sound is the pump and the water stream, with audio hits at 0.41, 0.88 and 1.39s. It stops the scroll because the title promises a specific, craveable drink plus an ASMR experience, and an empty jar creates the 'watch it get built' curiosity. The pink payoff is withheld until the end.

beats.what: Water pumped into an empty blender jar, with the title overlay and 'asmr edition' tag.
Soft-serve mix poured from a carton in a thin yellow stream into the jar, with water droplets visible on the plastic.
Ladle digs into a freezer bin of frost-covered strawberries.
Strawberries tumble from the ladle into the jar.
Empty ladle over the jar, then a second freezer scoop of strawberries at 5.7.
Strawberries settle in the jar, then the ladle digs into frozen banana slices (two alternating freezer/jar pairs through 9.57).
Banana slices drop into the jar on top of the red strawberries.
More bananas spooned in, then another scoop from the banana bin.
Handheld look at the loaded jar: layers of milky base, red berries and yellow bananas.
Measuring scoop digs into a jar of golden powder.
Powder scoop dumped into the jar.
Jar seated on the Vitamix base and the sound enclosure closed (14.6).
3.33s blending hold. The contents turn from chunky to an even pink as the timer counts 01:29 down to 01:25.
Whipped cream scooped on a twisted bar spoon and smeared onto the inside wall of the branded cup.
Cream spread in rings up the cup wall, a 1.73s shot.
Blender jar tilts and thick hot-pink smoothie starts pouring into the cream-lined cup.
A heavy ribbon of pink folds into the cup and pink-white spirals form behind the BLENDZ logo.
Cup on a marble counter with the lid pressed on by hand. At about 26.3 the hand lifts away to leave the finished swirled cup, which holds near-still to the end.

study.how_food_is_shown: Almost everything is shot at eye level or a slight high angle, close (the jar or cup fills 60-80% of the frame), on a handheld phone. Freezer scoops are shot looking down into the bins, so the frosty strawberries and bananas fill the frame. Gloved hands are in nearly every shot, which signals real shop hygiene and process. The light is natural daylight from the shop windows, neutral to slightly cool, with no steam (it's a cold drink). Frost on the freezer walls and condensation droplets on the jar sell 'cold and fresh'. Backgrounds are real working stations: dispensers, stainless counters, the Vitamix, spoon caddies. The finale moves to a cleaner marble counter with the purple BLENDZ wall sign out of focus behind the cup. Color emphasis builds from muted (clear water, beige mix) to vivid red fruit, then to the saturated pink-and-white finale, so the last shots are the most colorful in the video.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0-1.67s: water stream into the jar, close, normal speed. 1.67-3.0s: thin yellow soft-serve mix stream from the carton, a 1.33s close-up of the stream against droplet-covered plastic. 3.0-9.57s: alternating close-ups of the ladle scooping frosty strawberries (3.0, 5.7) and bananas (about 6.9, 8.93), with fruit dropping into the jar (3.93, 5.7, 7.77, 9.97). Each is 0.6-1.2s at normal speed, close enough to read the ice crystals. 12.13-13.53s: macro-ish close-up of the measuring scoop digging into the golden powder, then the drop into the jar (0.77s and 0.63s). 18.67-21.33s: whipped cream smeared on the cup wall with a twisted spoon, held 2.66s across two shots, close at cup height. 21.33-24.4s: the main pour, 3.07s across two shots, eye level at cup height, with the cup filling about 40% of the frame and the jar mouth at top. The thick pink purée slides out as a heavy ribbon and the swirl lines form against the cream. It plays at real speed; the slowness comes from the thick texture. 24.4-27.8s: the finished cup with lid, held 3.4s.
study.money_shot: The pour of thick pink smoothie into the cream-lined cup, from 21.33s and peaking at about 23.3-23.9s, when the heavy pink ribbon folds in and the candy-stripe spirals show behind the logo. That is roughly 77-86% through the video, and the pour as a whole runs 3.07s. It is set up by 18.67-21.33s of white cream being smeared on the walls (you see the 'canvas' first) and by the 3.33s blend that turns the fruit pink. Before that, 15s of muted prep keep the vivid color in reserve. It is followed by the lid going on and a 3.4s hero hold of the finished striped cup.
study.pacing: Two speeds. From 0 to about 15.3s it moves fast: 15 shots, mostly 0.63-1.43s, with a median of 1.13s, cutting back and forth between freezer bin and blender jar so every ingredient gets its own scoop-and-drop beat. Cuts land on scoop and drop sounds: audio hits at 3.12, 4.0, 4.96, 5.79, 6.56, 10.76, 13.58 and 14.77 sit within about 0.1-0.2s of the cuts at 3.0, 3.93, 5.03, 5.7, 6.53, 10.7, 13.53 and 14.6. From 15.33s it slows into longer holds: the blend runs 3.33s, the cream smear 0.93 + 1.73s, the pour 1.5 + 1.57s, and the finale 3.4s. Motion drops to match, from roughly 20-45 in the prep to 5-13 in the pour and 3.4-3.6 at 26.5-27.5s. Overall that's 21 shots in 27.8s (7.2 cuts per 10s), front-loaded so the ingredients fly by and the payoff gets room.
study.speed: Everything appears to play at normal speed, and I'm fairly confident of that. The pour looks slow because the purée is thick, not because of slow motion; motion during the pour stays a steady 9.6-13.5 with no ramp. The blender timer goes from about 01:29 to 01:25 over the 3.33s blend shot, which is consistent with real time, or at most a very slight speed-up. I see no timelapse or speed ramps.
study.on_screen_text: A two-line title from 0 to about 3.0s, gone by the first freezer shot. Line 1 is 'Strawberry Banana Smoothie' in heavy bold white sans-serif, title case, with a soft dark drop shadow, centered a little above mid-frame. Line 2 is '✨asmr edition✨' in a lighter-weight white lowercase sans with sparkle emojis, directly below. That's six words in total, shown all at once and static. There is no other overlay text, and no prices.
study.audio: No voice and no clearly audible music. The track is the in-shop ASMR: pump and water stream, carton pour, ladle scraping frozen fruit, fruit thudding into the jar, scoop clinks, the blender lid and enclosure clunk, then the blender running. Strong transient hits cluster between 0.41 and 16.01s, matching the scoop, drop and clunk actions. After 16s there are no strong hits, so the cream smear, pour and lid section is softer and smoother. The sound lines up with the picture because each cut lands on an action sound.
study.transitions: Hard cuts only. Most are action-to-action cuts that alternate locations: freezer-scoop to jar-drop at 3.93, 5.7, 7.77 and 9.57. Some read almost like match cuts on the ladle, with the scoop leaving the bin and arriving over the jar. There are no whips, zooms or flashes.
study.effects: Minimal. There may be a mild saturation and contrast lift that makes the reds and pinks pop, but no visible push-ins, shakes, glows, light leaks, freeze frames or split screens. Framing changes come from handheld camera moves, not digital zooms.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, H.264 at about 5.7 Mbps. That's reasonably clean, but the image is soft, with mild compression and some motion blur in the fast scoop shots. Everything is handheld with small wobbles, exposure is natural window light with a few bright patches on stainless and plastic, and color is neutral and true. It looks like an authentic phone shot inside a real shop rather than a studio: gloves, real freezers, real equipment. That honesty builds trust. The finale looks more premium because of the clean marble counter, the blurred branded wall and the vivid striped cup.
study.ending: It ends on the finished product. The lid goes on at 24.4s, the hand lifts away at about 26.3s, and the striped cup holds near-still (motion 3.4-3.6) for about 1.3-1.5s before the cut at 27.8s. There is no CTA, bite or sip. The end on a static hero, against the opening's empty jar, loops reasonably well back to the start of the build.
study.why_viral: 1) A visual payoff that's held back until the end: 15s of beige and red ingredients, then the vivid pink-and-white candy-stripe pour, which makes viewers wait for and rewatch the swirl. 2) ASMR texture and sound: frosty fruit, scoop scrapes and drops cut right on the sounds, with the 'asmr edition' title setting that expectation. 3) Fast, satisfying process rhythm (about 1.1s shots) showing real ingredients going in, which builds trust and makes viewers feel they could order exactly this. 4) A branded cup with the logo at the center of the money shot turns the swirl into a recognizable signature drink.
lessons: Put a 2-line title on screen for the first 2-3s: the drink name in heavy white bold with a shadow, plus a lighter tag like 'asmr edition'. Keep it to about 6 words and remove it before the first ingredient shot.
Open on an empty vessel and hold back the hero color until the last 20-25% of the video; the payoff should be the most saturated shot you have.
Cut prep at 0.6-1.4s per shot (median about 1.1s) and alternate source shot and destination shot (bin to scoop to drop into jar) so each ingredient becomes its own beat.
Place cuts on action sounds such as scoop scrapes, fruit drops and lid clunks, within about 0.15s of the hit, and keep the natural sound with no voiceover for ASMR builds.
Switch to long holds for the payoff: give the transformation (blend) about 3s, the build-up (cream smear) about 2.5s, the pour about 3s across 2 angles and the final hero 3-3.5s.
Show the 'canvas' before the pour, such as cream on the cup walls or a sauce-lined glass, so viewers anticipate the pattern the pour will create.
Shoot pours at cup height and eye level with the vessel filling about 40% of the frame, and play thick pours at real speed so the viscosity reads as indulgent.

End on a clean, static branded hero: move the finished product to the cleanest surface you have, with the shop sign blurred behind, let the hand leave frame and hold 1-1.5s of stillness before cutting.
Keep gloves, frost and condensation in frame; they read as fresh, cold and hygienic, which matters more than polish for a café's own footage.

study.format: Product showcase / menu montage set to a trending meme audio: rapid close-up cuts of a crêpe shop's finished desserts, mostly in takeout packaging, with light topping action.
