study.ending: It ends on the finished Tropical Mango hero shot (13.6–14.6s, 1.0s), with warm pendant lights blurred behind. The cut comes about 0.7s after the final word 'favorite' (13.92s), so there is no CTA or bite/sip. Because the joke is endless indecision, the end loops naturally back to 'okay let me tell you…' and the Matchanana, which encourages rewatches.
study.why_viral: 1) A relatable, funny hook: 'what's your fav?' answered by someone who keeps changing their mind turns a menu showcase into a skit and invites viewers to comment their own pick. 2) Four visually distinct, saturated drinks in 14.6s (pastel green, whipped tan, caramel gold, mango orange), so every 2.7–4.1s there is a new color hit. 3) Indulgent process moments: banana topping, caramel drizzle over a streaked glass, the bright mango pour. Each is paired with a hero shot in an attractive branded space. 4) Short, cut-on-beat pacing with a seamless loop drives completion and replays.
lessons: Open on hands already adding a topping or drizzle at 0.0s with the voice or audio starting at 0.00. Never open on an empty cup or a logo.
For multi-item menu drops, give each item 2.5–4s, structured as one process shot (topping, drizzle, pour or shake) and then one hero shot of the finished item in the space.

Use a two-line text overlay at about 50% frame height: line 1 is a constant question ('what's your fav ___?'), line 2 swaps to name each item exactly on its first cut. Keep each line to about 5–7 words.
Cut on the audio hits and the voice's turning points ('wait', 'no hold on', 'hmm'). Aim for about 1.0–1.9s shots, median about 1.3s, roughly 6–7 cuts per 10s.
Put your most indulgent texture (a thick drizzle, glossy sauce or streaked glass) around 40–55% of the runtime, hold it 1.5–2s, and follow it with a pulled-back hero shot.
Order items for color contrast (e.g. green, then tan, then caramel, then orange) so each new segment is a visual reset. Push the grade slightly warm and boost yellows and oranges.
Always turn branded cups or packaging logo-forward and shoot heroes with shallow depth of field against recognizable décor (neon sign, pendant lights) for brand recall.
Speed up the final segment (shots under 1.2s), end on a clean hero shot about 0.5–1s after the last word, and skip the CTA so the video loops back to the hook.

study.format: Restaurant promo / 'coming soon' teaser built as a meme-to-food bait-and-switch: 5s of found home-video comedy, then sizzling flat-top close-ups, then a plated hero shot with a branded address card.
study.item: Snow crab clusters and legs. They are glazed in butter and dusted heavily with orange-red Cajun/Old Bay-style seasoning, then seared on a flat-top griddle in bubbling seasoned butter. The ends show cracked, snowy white meat. Visual pull comes from the saturated orange-red shells against white flesh, gritty seasoning texture, glossy butter, bubbling fat and a final white plate with a lemon half.
study.hook: Frame one (0.0s) is not food at all. It is a cluttered home kitchen with three middle-aged men around a stockpot, a big white bucket and a black tub, with open Tostitos and Doritos bags on the counter. It reads like an old viral home video. The first words are 'What up, guys?' at 1.33s. It stops the scroll because it looks like a relatable meme clip rather than an ad, and the bucket/tub creates mild curiosity about what is being handled. The payoff comes at ~5.0s: the middle man recoils and yells, and it hard-cuts straight to sizzling crab.

beats.what: Found-footage home kitchen: three men around a pot and white bucket, chip bags on the counter. 'What up, guys?' at 1.33s.
The man on the right reaches into the black tub and handles something (likely the crabs) while the middle man seasons/measures over the pot.
The middle man jerks back, laughing/yelling. This is the comedic beat that sets up the cut.
Hard cut to a macro of a seasoned crab cluster on the griddle, coated in dry rub, with an orange butter pool bubbling.
The same shot widens slightly to clusters searing on the flat-top, with seasoning powder and butter sizzling.
Close-up of snow crab legs and a cluster with cracked white meat, sparkling with seasoning. Voice: 'From Kentucky, welcome to D.C...'
Low, eye-level side view of a stacked cluster: glossy orange shell with exposed white meat in front and the griddle surface below. The steadiest food shot.
0.53s flash of crab legs sitting in foaming, bubbling butter on the griddle.
Macro of a cluster's white meat end, heavily seasoned. Ends in a bright light-leak flash. Voice: 'number two.'
Plated crab legs with a lemon half on a white plate, overlaid with 'COMING SOON / Omars Seafood & Grill / 26751 Brookpark Rd Ext / North Olmsted, OH'. Voice: 'Teach me how to do it.'
The branded card settles to full saturation and holds on the plate until the end at 14.4s.

study.how_food_is_shown: Two very different looks. The kitchen clip (0-5s) is a static-ish eye-level wide in flat indoor window light, deliberately low-fi. The food footage (5-11.73s) is all handheld macro or very close range, inches from the griddle. Angles vary: 45° down onto clusters at 5.0s and 7.13s, and a low, near-tabletop eye level at 8.47s that makes the cluster look tall and sculptural, with a dark blurred background. No hands appear in the food shots. The griddle's dark steel and speckled seasoning residue frame the orange shells. Lighting is warm and punchy and catches gloss on the butter and the sparkle of seasoning grains. The final shot (11.73s) switches to a clean bright-white backdrop and white plate, slightly overhead at ~30-45°, with a lemon as the only prop. It is pure contrast: red food, white everything else.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 5.0-7.13s (2.13s): macro on a rub-coated cluster, with the frame filled by seasoning texture and an orange butter puddle bubbling at the lower right. It drifts and widens slightly at normal speed. 7.13-8.47s (1.33s): tight close-up on legs and the white meat end of a cluster, seasoning glittering, handheld drift. 8.47-10.13s (1.67s): low side-angle close-up of the cluster's cracked white meat under glossy orange shell. This is the longest and steadiest food hold (motion drops to 8-13). 10.13-10.67s (0.53s): close-up of legs sitting in foaming, bubbling butter, the 'sizzle' moment. 10.67-11.73s (1.07s): macro of the meat end of a cluster, then washed out by the light leak. There are no pours, cheese pulls or bites. The liquid action is the bubbling butter at 5.0s and 10.13s. Everything appears to play at roughly normal speed.
study.money_shot: 8.47-10.13s (59-70% of the video), held 1.67s. It is the low eye-level side view of a seasoned snow crab cluster with the cracked, flaky white meat facing camera and glossy orange-red shell stacked behind. It is set up by two closer, shakier griddle shots (5.0s and 7.13s) that show texture but not form, so this steadier, lower angle reads as the 'reveal' of the whole piece. It is followed by a quick 0.53s bubbling-butter cut and a 1.07s macro, then the plated hero shot with the brand card. The plated shot is the secondary money shot and gets the longest hold of any food: 2.67s.
study.pacing: Two halves. First comes one long 5.0s unbroken found-footage shot (35% of runtime) with low motion (4-9 out of 100) to let the comedy play out. Then come fast food cuts: 2.13s, 1.33s, 1.67s, 0.53s and 1.07s (median 1.67s), with motion jumping to 17-43 from handheld macro movement. It ends with a 2.67s hold on the branded plate. Overall 4.17 cuts per 10s. Audio hits after 5.0s arrive roughly every 0.35-0.7s (5.58, 5.93, 6.64, 6.99, 7.70, 8.22, 8.40...), suggesting a beat or rhythmic sizzle. Cuts land only loosely on them: 8.47 sits near 8.40, 10.67 near 10.52, and 11.73 between 11.58 and 11.92. The rhythm is a slow setup followed by an accelerating burst (cuts shrink from 2.13s to 0.53s) and a resolving hold.
study.speed: None clearly detectable. All food footage looks like normal-speed handheld. The seasoning and butter bubbling do not show the smooth, smeared motion of true slow-mo, and no speed ramps show within a shot (moderate confidence). The motion spike to 43.2 at ~14.0s is likely a slight zoom/drift on the final card, not a speed change.
study.on_screen_text: Only on the final shot, from 11.73s to the end (14.4s). It fades in through the light-leak transition: washed-out pink at 11.73s, fully saturated by ~12.2s. There are four lines, centered in the top third. 'COMING SOON' is in bold blocky red sans caps. 'Omars' is a large red retro script with a white inner stroke, black outline and red outer glow. 'Seafood & Grill' is a smaller red script. '26751 BROOKPARK RD EXT' and 'NORTH OLMSTED, OH' are in red block caps with black stroke. About 10 words appear at once. The text sits over the white background and the top of the plate, so it reads cleanly. No prices and no text during the food or meme shots.
study.audio: The original audio from the kitchen meme clip carries over the whole video. It is dialogue in a Southern/joking register: 'What up, guys?' (1.33-2.09s), 'From Kentucky, welcome to D.C., number two.' (7.04-11.80s) and 'Teach me how to do it.' (11.88-13.00s). The speech keeps running under the crab footage, so the humor continues into the food section and the last line ('Teach me how to do it') lands on the brand card. The regular audio hits after 5s point to a rhythmic bed (music beat or sizzle), but this can't be confirmed from the data. No voiceover from the restaurant and no added sound effects are evident.
study.transitions: 5.0s: hard cut from the man's recoil in the kitchen to a crab macro, the bait-and-switch. 7.13s, 8.47s, 10.13s and 10.67s: hard cuts between griddle shots. 11.73s: a bright light-leak/flash transition. The last food frame blows out to warm white-gold with lens flare and bokeh orbs, then the plated shot fades in still partly washed out, and the text glows into full saturation by ~12.2s.
study.effects: The food shots have a strong warm, saturated grade: oranges and reds pushed hard, contrast up, some sharpening that makes the seasoning grains sparkle. A light leak/flare overlay at ~11.5-12.0s bridges into the end card. The end card has bright, lifted whites and saturated reds, with a possible slow push-in/drift ending in the motion spike at ~14.0s. The kitchen clip is left ungraded and slightly soft, which reinforces its found-footage feel.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264, ~5.5 Mbps. The kitchen clip is visibly low-res and soft, being repurposed old footage. The food clips are sharper, close-focus phone footage. They are handheld and drifting rather than stabilized, with good exposure and heavy saturation. Mixing lo-fi meme footage with crisp, graded macro food makes the food feel higher-end by contrast. The bright white studio-style plate shot is the most 'professional' frame and is reserved for the brand card.
study.ending: It ends on the finished plated crab legs under the 'COMING SOON' brand and address card, held 2.67s (11.73-14.4s). The dialogue line 'Teach me how to do it' finishes at 13.00s, leaving ~1.4s of pure card hold. It does not loop seamlessly; the final frame (plated food) is very different from the opening kitchen.
study.why_viral: 1) Bait-and-switch: it opens like a funny home-video meme, so viewers don't skip it as an ad, and the recoil at 5.0s hard-cuts straight into sizzling crab. 2) Extreme color and texture: saturated orange-red shells, gritty rub, bubbling butter and snowy white meat in tight macro trigger appetite instantly. 3) The meme audio keeps playing over the food, so the humor and the craving stack rather than compete. 4) A clear local hook at the end (coming soon, exact address) turns hunger into a destination.
lessons: Lead with 3-5s of something that doesn't look like an ad (a meme, a relatable moment, staff banter), then hard-cut to food on a visual peak like a reaction or flinch.
Once the food starts, cut fast: keep griddle/sizzle shots at 0.5-2.1s each and shorten them as you approach the end (here 2.13 → 1.33 → 1.67 → 0.53 → 1.07s).

Shoot proteins in macro, inches away, and include at least one low eye-level side angle that shows cut-open interior (white meat, crumb, cheese) against the glossy exterior. Make that your steadiest, ~1.5-2s hold.
Include a 0.5s 'sizzle insert' of bubbling butter/oil to sell heat and freshness even without audio.
Push warm saturation and sharpening on seasoned or fried food so spice grains sparkle and reds/oranges pop, but keep the end-card plate on a bright white background for maximum contrast.
Use a light-leak or flash transition to move from raw cooking footage into the polished hero plate. It signals 'the reveal' and lets the brand text glow in.
Put the CTA text in only the final 2.5-3s, in the top third over empty background, as name + 'COMING SOON'/offer + exact address, with a heavy outline and glow so it reads at a glance.
Let a funny or memorable audio line land on the end card (here 'Teach me how to do it' at 11.88s) so the brand reveal coincides with the punchline.

study.format: Restaurant behind-the-counter plating / product showcase: final garnish on a takeout bowl, then a handheld orbit of the finished dish, with a short first-person 'obsessed' voiceover line and karaoke captions.
study.item: A loaded fajita-style takeout bowl from Fatima's Grill: charred grilled shrimp, sliced steak, long strips of bright green bell pepper and onion over rice with a red-orange sauce. It is topped with shredded white cheese, a bundle of magenta pickled red onion, white-and-pink radish slices, yellow banana-pepper rings and a lemon wedge. It works on camera because of the color blocking (orange, green, magenta, white, yellow) in a black container, the visible grill char on the shrimp and meat, and how overfilled it looks.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0.0s) is an extreme close, slightly high-angle shot of a black-gloved hand laying a strip of magenta pickled onion onto the bowl. Shredded cheese and radish are in the foreground and the heaped steak, shrimp and peppers sit behind. The first word, 'I'm', is spoken at 0.00s, and bold white caps 'I'M IN LOVE' appear immediately, with each word turning yellow as it's spoken. The scroll stops because the shot opens mid-action on the last finishing touch, the colors are already saturated, and the line is emotional and personal with no setup. The hand then lifts away at ~1.3s to reveal the full bowl.

beats.what: Gloved hand places pickled red onion on the bowl, close up. VO 'I'm in love' with karaoke caption.
Hand pulls out of frame and the whole heaped bowl sits in frame on the stainless prep line. VO 'I'm obsessed'.
A gloved hand enters top-right with a lemon wedge and squeezes it over the bowl (~3.4s). VO 'and I don't even feel guilty'.
Hand sweeps in from the left and tucks the lemon wedge into the side of the bowl, then adjusts the onion and cheese garnish (to 4.7s). VO 'about it' ends at 4.42s.
Cut on an audio hit to a low, close handheld angle from the left side of the bowl showing shrimp, steak and peppers, camera moving.
Quick 0.57s shot: tight low angle on the shrimp-and-steak edge of the bowl, cutting board and prep bins behind.
Handheld arc from the right side across the charred shrimp, steak and pepper strips filling the frame, ending at the front with the cheese and radish.
Cut on an audio hit to a slightly wider 45° hero of the complete bowl, all garnishes visible, camera easing back. Video ends at 8.5s.

study.how_food_is_shown: Shot 1 is a locked, near-overhead ~45-60° close-up with the bowl filling the bottom two-thirds of the frame. Black nitrile gloves are in frame for half the shot, which reads as a professional kitchen and contrasts with the colorful food. Shots 2-5 are handheld low angles (roughly 20-35° above the rim), very close to the food, arcing around the bowl so the meat and shrimp tower toward the lens and look bigger. The background is the real stainless steel prep line with ingredient bins (green, purple, yellow) plus a white cutting board. That gives an authentic 'made right now at the counter' feel, though it's slightly cluttered. Lighting is bright overhead kitchen fluorescent, even and shadowless, so the colors read clean. The black container frames the colors. Texture emphasis is on the grill char and sear marks on the shrimp and steak, the glossy peppers, and the fluffy shredded cheese. No steam is visible.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0.0-1.2s: extreme close of the gloved hand placing pickled onion, about 1.2s at normal speed, showing the magenta onion against white cheese and orange sauce. ~3.2-3.6s: a lemon squeeze top-right, small in frame, not given a dedicated close-up. 3.9-4.7s: hand close in the left foreground setting the lemon wedge and fluffing the garnish, ~0.8s. 4.7-5.47s and 5.47-6.03s: two very close low-angle moving shots of the char-marked shrimp and steak, 0.77s and 0.57s, normal speed. 6.03-7.47s: the longest close move (1.43s), arcing across the meat and peppers so they fill most of the frame. There are no drips, pulls or cut-opens. The appetite appeal comes from char texture and color rather than liquid.
study.money_shot: The arcing close-up of the charred shrimp, seared steak and glossy green pepper strips from 6.03s to 7.47s (71%-88% of the video), held 1.43s, the longest shot after the opener. It is set up by the slow 4.7s finishing-touch opener, then two fast 0.77s and 0.57s close angles that build energy into it. It's followed by a 1.03s slightly wider hero frame of the whole bowl to close. Secondary reveal: the hand clearing frame at ~1.2-1.3s, when the full bowl is first seen (about 15%).
study.pacing: Two halves. The first 4.7s (55% of runtime) is a single continuous shot carried by the voiceover, with low motion (6.7-18.9) while the hand garnishes. Once the speech ends at 4.42s, the edit switches to fast cuts: shots of 0.77s, 0.57s, 1.43s and 1.03s, with motion jumping to 31-46. Median shot is 1.03s and the rate is 4.71 cuts per 10s. The cuts at 4.7, 6.03 and 7.47s land within ~0.06s of audio hits (4.69, 5.97, 7.49). The structure is: words over a calm build, then rhythm-cut camera moves as a visual payoff. The whole thing moves quickly and finishes in 8.5s.
study.speed: Most likely none. Hand movements in shot 1 look natural at real speed, and the high motion in shots 2-5 (31-46) comes from handheld camera arcs, not timelapse jumpiness. There's no sign of slow motion: no smooth low-motion liquid. Moderate confidence that shots 2-5 are at or near real speed; a slight speed-up of the orbits is possible but not evident.
study.on_screen_text: No standalone title, item name or price. The only overlay is the speech captions (see captions).
study.captions: Present from 0.0s to ~4.4s. Bold rounded sans-serif in all caps, white fill with a thick black stroke and shadow, centered in the upper-middle third (about 28-33% from the top), above the food and over the gloved hand and background. They show 2-3 words at a time ('I'M IN LOVE', 'I'M OBSESSED', 'AND I DON'T', 'EVEN FEEL GUILTY'), and the active word is highlighted yellow in karaoke sync with the word timings. They disappear when the voiceover ends, and the second half has no text.
study.audio: A short, energetic first-person voiceover line (13 words, 0.00-4.42s): 'I'm in love, I'm obsessed, and I don't even feel guilty about it.' It sounds like a trending sound or audio clip used as the hook. A music or beat bed runs under it, with regular hits at about 0.3-0.6s intervals (0.5, 0.97, 1.58, 1.91, 2.53 ... 8.0). After the voice ends, the beat carries the cut section, and cuts land on hits at 4.69, ~5.97 and 7.49. No food ASMR (sizzle or crunch) is evident.
study.transitions: Hard cuts only (4.7, 5.47, 6.03, 7.47s). The 6.03 cut is almost a match cut: the same right-side angle on the bowl continues and the camera keeps arcing, so it feels like one fluid move. The 4.7 and 7.47 cuts are beat-synced.
study.effects: No zooms added in post, no shake effects, flashes or freeze frames. All movement is real handheld camera motion: arcs and push-ins around the bowl in shots 2-5. The color grade is bright with boosted saturation and slight warmth. Greens, the magenta onion and the orange sauce pop, while stainless and white surfaces stay fairly neutral.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264 at ~4972 kbps. That's decent bitrate for 720p, so the food is reasonably sharp, though fine detail on the cheese shreds and char softens slightly in fast moves. Shot 1 is steady; shots 2-5 are handheld, smooth enough to look intentional and possibly phone-stabilized. Exposure is bright and even from kitchen fluorescents, with no blown highlights on the food and low noise. It reads as authentic in-house phone content rather than studio work. The styling (bright garnish color blocking, overfilled bowl, gloves) does the 'premium' work, while the prep-line background signals freshness and real portions.
study.ending: Ends on a slightly wider 45° hero of the finished, fully garnished bowl (7.47-8.5s, 1.03s hold), with the camera easing back slightly. It cuts about 0.5s after the beat hit at 8.0s, with no CTA or text. It loops cleanly back to the opening close-up of the same bowl being garnished, so a rewatch feels continuous.
study.why_viral: 1) Color blocking: magenta pickled onion, green peppers, orange rice/sauce, white cheese and radish, and yellow peppers in a black bowl look striking at thumbnail size. 2) Abundance and char: the bowl is heaped with visibly grilled shrimp and steak, and low close angles make it look huge and value-packed. 3) A relatable, trending-style 'I'm obsessed and not guilty' line with karaoke captions hooks from the first frame, at 0.0s. 4) The rhythm switch from a calm garnish to beat-cut orbit shots gives a payoff in under 9s, which drives rewatches and the loop.
lessons: Start talking or start the audio at 0.0s with captions on frame 1. Never open on silence or an empty plate; open mid-action on the final garnish.
Open on the last finishing touch, such as a garnish, squeeze or sprinkle, at close range, then pull the hand out within ~1.2-1.5s to reveal the full dish.
Keep the first shot long (~4-5s) while there's voiceover. Once speech ends, switch to fast 0.5-1.5s shots of camera moves so energy rises in the second half.
Snap cuts to beat hits within ~0.05s. Here 3 of 4 cuts land on audio peaks.

Shoot payoff angles low (20-35° above the rim) and close, arcing handheld around the dish so proteins tower toward the lens. Give the most textured area (char or sear) the longest of the fast shots (~1.4s).
Style for color contrast: add one or two bold accent garnishes (a pickled red onion bundle, radish, lemon, yellow peppers) so the dish reads at a glance. Dark containers make the colors pop.
Use karaoke captions: white bold all-caps with a black stroke, 2-3 words at a time, active word in yellow, in the upper-middle third so they don't cover the food.
End on a slightly wider hero of the complete dish, held ~1s, that matches the opening framing so the video loops seamlessly. Keep the total under ~9s.
Add a moderate saturation and warmth boost in the grade, but keep whites and stainless neutral so the kitchen still looks clean and real.

study.format: Menu showcase / 'choose your…' poll reel: a quick intro on the bubble-waffle iron, then 4 numbered finished desserts set to a trending sped-up song, so viewers comment their pick.
study.item: Hong Kong bubble waffles from a dessert café (@crepencrunch). Two are cones, two are flat plates. (1) A cone with strawberry ice cream, M&Ms, fresh strawberries and white-chocolate drizzle, very colourful. (2) A plate with chocolate/brownie ice cream, Kinder bars stood upright, white and milk chocolate drizzle and chocolate pearls. (3) A cone with vanilla ice cream, a chocolate-shaving crust, Kinder chunks and dark chocolate drizzle. (4) A plate with cookies-and-cream ice cream, a whole Oreo, Oreo crumbs and a thick chocolate sauce drizzle. They stand out for the golden puffy egg-bubble texture, glossy drizzles, and candy colour against cream ice cream, with a pink neon sign glowing in the background.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0–0.37s) is an out-of-focus macro of golden-orange waffle bubbles, just warm round shapes. The music starts on the first frame with the sped-up 'La La La' vocal ('About your new messiah…'). At 0.37s 'CHOOSE' pops up in bold white outlined caps while the shot racks into focus. By ~1.5s it reveals a fresh bubble waffle sitting on the open iron. The blurry warm blobs make you look to resolve the image, and the 'CHOOSE YOUR BUBBLE WAFFLE' text builds over ~2s. That sets up a game: watch all options, then pick one.

beats.what: Blurred macro of waffle bubbles, warm orange, with the music starting immediately.
Rack focus to sharp bubble waffle on the open iron with a steel lamp neck behind. Text builds word by word: CHOOSE (0.37), YOUR (~1.5), BUBBLE WAFFLE (~2.1).

Option '1': opens tight on the M&Ms, strawberries and white drizzle, then eases back to show the full cone with strawberry ice cream. Pink neon is behind it, and the camera is near-still (motion 4.6–6.7).
Option '2': a gloved hand pushes a Kinder bar upright into the chocolate ice cream, with a whipped-cream can soft in the background.
The camera moves fast and then settles, revealing the full flat plate: drizzled bubbles, chocolate pearls and two Kinder bars.
Option '3': extreme close-up of vanilla ice cream with dark chocolate drizzle, a chocolate-shaving crust and Kinder chunks (0.6s).
Pull-back to the whole option-3 cone in front of the pink neon sign, held nearly still (motion 7–9).
Option '4': the Oreo standing in cookies-and-cream ice cream under thick chocolate sauce. It starts soft and racks or slides into focus, then a slow lateral move continues to the end.

study.how_food_is_shown: Almost every shot is at eye level or a low angle on a long lens, with very shallow depth of field. Each dessert towers in the frame against a creamy blurred background of the café: a pink neon sign, a green plant wall and a white counter. Framing is tight; each dessert fills 70–100% of the vertical frame, and macros crop into a single scoop. Hands appear only once (the gloved hand at 6.07s, adding a Kinder bar). Lighting is bright, soft daylight from the side, which makes the drizzles shine and the waffle bubbles look golden. Colour comes from the toppings (red, green and yellow M&Ms, red strawberries, brown chocolate), set against white or pink ice cream. Props are minimal: paper cone wrappers, a white plate, and a whipped-cream can out of focus.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0–1.5s: macro of the waffle bubbles, defocused, racking to sharp. It plays at real speed and slowly, motion ~12–15. 3.73s: a very close macro on the M&Ms and white drizzle of option 1, then an easy pull to the full cone by ~4.6s, held still until 6.07s (~1.5s static hold). 6.07–7.0s: medium close-up of a gloved hand pressing a Kinder bar into the ice cream (0.93s). It may be slightly slowed, but I'm not sure. 8.87–9.47s: the tightest shot in the video, a macro of the chocolate drizzle dripping over the vanilla scoop and the shaving crust (0.6s). 11.0–13.6s: close-up of the Oreo and sauce-glazed scoops, starting soft and sliding into sharp focus. There are no live pours, cheese-pull equivalents or cut-opens; every drizzle is already set.
study.money_shot: Option 1's full cone at ~4.4–6.07s (≈32–45% of the video). It has the most colour: the pink scoop, rainbow M&Ms, red strawberries and dripping white chocolate in a crisp golden cone, with pink neon behind. It's set up by the tight macro at 3.73s, which lands right on an audio hit (3.68s) and then pulls back. It holds about 1.5–2s nearly still (motion 4.6–6.7), then hard-cuts to the action of the hand placing the Kinder bar.
study.pacing: Fast and music-driven: 8 detected shots in 13.6s (5.15 cuts/10s, median 1.64s). There is also an apparent extra change to option 4 at ~11.0s (motion jumps from 8.8 to 64.3) that the cut list doesn't show. The intro is the longest shot (3.37s), so the text can build. After that, each option gets about 2.3–2.8s, split into a fast detail shot (0.6–0.93s) followed by a calmer reveal or hold (1.4–2.7s). The rhythm alternates between a high-motion move (motion 35–69 at 3.5–4.0, 6.0–7.5, 8.5–9.5, 11.0–11.5) and a still hold (4.6–6.7 at 4.5–5.5, 7–9 at 10–10.5). The 3.73 cut sits 0.05s after a hit at 3.68. Others land within ~0.15–0.25s of hits (7.0 vs 7.17, 10.87 vs 11.1), so cuts follow the beat loosely rather than frame-accurately.
study.speed: There are no timelapses. The footage looks like gimbal moves at normal or slightly slowed speed, and the song itself is a sped-up version. Within shots, motion spikes and then drops: 68.7 to 20.2 inside the 7.0–8.87 shot, and 64.3 down to 19.8 in the option-4 segment. This looks like speed ramps or eased fast moves into a slow settle (moderate confidence). The hand placing the Kinder bar at 6.07–7.0 may be mild slow motion (low confidence). The opening rack focus plays at real speed.
study.on_screen_text: Intro title: 'CHOOSE' / 'YOUR' / 'BUBBLE WAFFLE'. It is heavy white sans-serif in all caps with a thick black outline, centred in the upper-middle of the frame and stacked on 4 lines. It builds one word or line at a time: CHOOSE at 0.37s, YOUR by ~1.5s, BUBBLE WAFFLE by ~2.1s. It stays until the cut at 3.73s, with up to 4 words on screen. After that, a single numeral '1', '2', '3' or '4' sits dead centre (~57% down), in the same white bold style with a dark outline. Each numeral stays for that whole option: 1 from 3.73–6.07, 2 from 6.07–8.87, 3 from 8.87–~11.0, 4 from ~11.0 to the end. There are no prices or item names.
study.captions: none. The 13 transcribed words are lyrics from the backing song ('About your new messiah, cause your theories catch fire / And they confine your…'), not speech.
study.audio: Trending music only: a sped-up version of 'La La La' (Naughty Boy ft. Sam Smith). Vocals start at 0.00s. There is no voiceover and no ASMR food sound. Audio hits fall roughly every 0.2–0.45s (0.19, 0.63, 1.06 … 12.41), and option changes sit on or near them (3.68 to cut 3.73; 7.17 to 7.0). The intro text builds on the vocal phrases.
study.transitions: Hard cuts between all shots. The opening uses a cut at 0.37s from a blurred frame to a blurred frame plus title, then an in-shot rack focus that works as a 'reveal' transition. The switch from option 3 to option 4 at ~11.0s isn't in the cut list but shows a big motion spike, likely a fast move or blur that the detector missed. Within each option there is a detail-to-wide pairing (macro then pull-back) that works like a punch-out jump cut.
study.effects: Rack focus or defocus-to-sharp at 0–1.5s and at the start of option 4. Shallow depth of field throughout, with bokeh on the neon and greenery. The grade is warm and saturated (golden waffles, punchy reds and pinks) with moderate contrast and slight sharpening that gives some edge halos. No freeze frames, split screens, shakes or light leaks.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, h264, ~5.3 Mbps. That is decent but softer than native 1080p, with mild compression and over-sharpening visible on textures. The camera moves are gimbal-smooth with no handheld shake. Exposure is bright and even, there's no visible noise, and white ice cream isn't clipped. The high-end feel comes from the long-lens shallow depth of field, the neon-sign brand background and careful plating. The modest resolution doesn't hurt it at phone size.
study.ending: It ends on option 4, the Oreo dessert, partway through a slow lateral move about 2.6s into that segment. There's no bite, reaction or CTA text. The 'choose' premise is the built-in CTA, prompting viewers to comment 1–4. The music cuts mid-phrase, so it loops easily back to the blurry opening.
study.why_viral: 1) The 'Choose your…' numbered format turns a menu into a game, so people watch to the end and comment their number, which boosts engagement. 2) Four towering desserts with extreme topping colour (M&Ms, Kinder, Oreo, glossy drizzle) shown in macro then wide give a fast run of visual rewards about every 2.5s. 3) A trending sped-up song with cuts near its beats keeps the energy high. 4) The blurry-to-sharp opening and the word-by-word title make the viewer resolve the image in the first 1–2s.
lessons: Frame a menu as a choice: put 'CHOOSE YOUR [ITEM]' up in the first 0.4s, then show 3–5 options numbered with one big centred digit. It drives comments and watch-through.
Give each option about 2.3–2.8s, split into a fast macro detail (0.6–0.9s) then a pull-back or still hold (1.4–2s) of the whole item.
Open on a defocused macro of the product's most recognisable texture and rack to sharp within about 1.5s, so viewers stay to see what it is.
Build title text one word or line at a time on the music beats (about every 0.5–1s), in bold white caps with a thick black outline, centred upper-middle.
Shoot at eye level on a long lens with shallow depth of field, and put a branded neon sign or colourful wall in the blurred background. The item should fill 70–100% of the frame height.
Put the most colourful item first (here, option 1 at 27% of the video) and hold it nearly still for about 1.5s. The first reward should be the strongest.
Alternate high-motion moves (gimbal swoops or speed-ramped pushes) with still holds, and cut within about 0.1–0.25s of strong beats in a trending sped-up song.
Without ASMR, let a trending track carry the audio. Keep text to one numeral per option and skip prices, so the food stays the focus.
End mid-move on the last option without an outro, so the poll question works as the CTA and the video loops.

study.format: Promo / brand announcement montage: a menu sizzle reel of making-of shots (drizzles, pours, toppings) and finished-item reveals, cut to a trending rap track. It announces a new location ('we're coming to Strongsville').
study.item: CREPEscape dessert-shop menu. It includes a crepe with a feathered dark and white chocolate pattern, fanned strawberries and banana coins; an Oreo bubble-waffle sundae cup; a Fruity Pebbles milkshake with a whipped-cream tower; a strawberry, chocolate and pistachio cup topped with shredded kataifi; fruit-shaped mousse desserts (apple, banana, mango, raspberry); crepe sticks with Fruity Pebbles, pistachio and Oreo crumble; and a tiger-striped brown-sugar boba milk tea. The visual draw is high contrast: the zebra/feather chocolate pattern, glossy drizzles, rainbow cereal against white cream, pistachio green against chocolate brown, and syrup 'tiger stripes' inside clear cups.
study.hook: Frame 1 (0-~1s) is a low, eye-level macro of the crepe plate. Glossy fanned strawberries sit in front of a feathered chocolate/white-chocolate pattern, with shallow depth of field. By ~1.4s the screen becomes a 3-panel split of strawberries, a toothpick dragging the feather pattern, and banana slices. Script text builds word by word: 'You really / About to / Do it?' Then from ~2.3s comes 'Yes, we're coming to Strongsville'. The first sound is the instantly recognizable 'Not Like Us' track, with lyrics starting at 1.77s. It stops the scroll through a hypnotic pattern-drag motion, a triple-image density that reads like 'there's a lot here', a trending song, and a local-news tease for a specific town.

beats.what: Full-frame macro of the feathered chocolate crepe with fanned strawberries, then a 3-panel split screen.
Middle panel: a toothpick drags through dark/white chocolate lines to make the feather pattern. Text 'You really About to Do it?'
Announcement text 'Yes, we're coming to Strongsville' over the split screen (to ~4.8s).

Triptych of the Oreo sundae: white-chocolate drizzle, a gloved hand placing an Oreo, chocolate drizzle and crumbs. Text 'You really About to Do it?' then 'Cleveland's #1 Dessert Shop'.
Text 'Can't Fake Influence' lands in sync with the lyric 'fake influence' (8.51-8.73s).
Whipped cream sprayed onto the Fruity Pebbles shake, with a rainbow lens flare.
Close push on the cereal-crusted whipped cream and the speckled shake.
Thin stream of milk chocolate pours onto strawberries in a clear cup.
Pistachio drizzle, then a scoop of pistachio ice cream is dropped in. At ~14.4s chocolate drips down whole strawberries; text 'Find' begins.
Finished strawberry, chocolate and pistachio cup with kataifi crunch, swirled sides, against a wood-slat backdrop. Text 'Find Your Escape'. A near-still hold.
Rack-focus across the fruit-shaped mousse desserts, with crepe sticks in the foreground.
Pistachio crumbs scooped onto a drizzled crepe stick; white chocolate drizzled over a Fruity Pebbles stick.
Oreo crumble shaken over a chocolate-drizzled stick. Lineup of three toppings at ~20-21.5s.
Brown-sugar syrup squeezed around the inside of a clear cup. At 22.07s milk tea is poured/stirred in.
Boba cup rotated against black and wood stripes, showing tiger-stripe syrup and pearls (to 24.77s).
Gloved hand sprays whipped cream onto the Oreo sundae.
Fruity Pebbles rain onto a piped whipped-cream tower (low-motion, near-still shot).
Boba cup with CREPEscape logo sticker, on an audio hit.
Table spread, then the shake. Text 'They / Not / Like / Us' builds word by word, matching the lyric (29.74-31.42s).
Out-of-focus strawberry cup and shake, pulling into focus.
High-angle sliding shot of the mousse fruits and crepe-stick platter.
Hero group shot: shake and strawberry cup with logo, crepe stick blurred in the foreground.
Group shot continues, then a slide across the crepe plate on a marble table.

study.how_food_is_shown: Almost everything is at eye level or a slight 45° angle, very close (macro to medium-close), with shallow depth of field. Backgrounds melt into bokeh of a warm wood-slat wall, dark kitchen or white marble. A few high-angle slides (33.6-35.5s) show the platter layout. Hands appear only in black nitrile gloves, which keeps them graphic and clean and makes white cream and colorful toppings pop. Lighting is bright, soft and even (studio/window), with specular highlights on chocolate and sauces. Props are minimal: clear branded cups with a pink logo sticker, white plates and marble. The edit stresses contrast: zebra chocolate lines, rainbow cereal on white, green pistachio on brown chocolate, syrup stripes behind clear plastic.
study.close_ups_and_pours: 0-4.8s: macro split screen. A toothpick drags the chocolate feather pattern in the middle panel the whole time, while the strawberry and banana panels slowly drift. 5.97-9.53s: triptych macros of white-chocolate drizzle on Oreo ice cream, an Oreo pressed in, and chocolate ribbons with crumbs (about 3.5s total). 9.53-10.7s: whipped cream spray in close-up (1.17s). 10.7-11.8s: cereal-topped cream macro (1.1s). 11.8-13.0s: thin chocolate stream onto strawberries, smooth and glossy (1.2s), and likely slowed. ~12.5-13s: pistachio drizzle zig-zag. 13.0-~14s: ice cream scoop release. ~14.2-15.3s: chocolate drip down whole strawberries with a thin pour stream. ~18.9-19.6s: pistachio crumbs falling from a scoop, then a white-chocolate drizzle stream onto a Fruity Pebbles stick. 19.63-~20s: Oreo crumble shaken off a scoop. ~21.5-22.07s: syrup squeezed down the inside of the cup, then the milk tea stir at 22.07s. 22.07-24.77s: rotating cup showing tiger stripes. 24.77-26.87s: whipped cream rosette sprayed (2.1s). 26.87-28.5s: cereal raining on the cream tower, a near-still 1.63s hold. Each close-up lasts 1-2.4s; none longer than 2.97s.
study.money_shot: The finished strawberry, chocolate and pistachio cup at 15.3s (34% in), held to 17.43s (2.13s). Motion drops to 6-10 at 15.5-16.5s, so it is nearly static and lets the eye read it. It is built up over the 3.5s before: chocolate pour on strawberries (11.8s), pistachio drizzle and scoop (13.0s), chocolate dripping over the strawberries (14.4s). It is followed by the brand line 'Find Your Escape' and a rack-focus to the fruit mousses. A close second is the opening feather-pattern drag, which works as the hook.
study.pacing: Fast and even. There are 25 shots in 44.6s (5.38 cuts per 10s), with a median shot of 1.87s, ranging from 1.03s to 2.97s. There are no long ASMR holds. The 'holds' are just 2-2.4s on finished items (15.3s, 19.63s, 22.07s, 38.0s) and the white text card (40.4-42.27s). The busiest stretch is 9.53-13.0s, four shots of about 1.1-1.3s each. Cuts mostly ride the song's bounce. Clear cut-to-hit matches include 22.07 (hit 22.26), 28.5 (hit 28.51) and 42.27 (hit 42.27). Text reveals match lyric words ('fake influence' 8.5s; 'They not like us' 29.7-31.4s). Overall it moves briskly and like a music video.
study.speed: Probable mild slow motion (about 50-60%, moderate confidence) on the sauce pours and drizzles at 11.8-15.3s and ~18.9-20s; the streams look smooth and unbroken. The cereal fall at 26.87-28.5s also reads as slow motion (motion 4-9 while particles drift). No obvious speed ramps or timelapses; the rotating boba cup and push-ins play near real time.
study.on_screen_text: Elegant script/calligraphy font in two colors: small white script with a dark drop shadow for lead-in words, and large hot-magenta script with a grey offset shadow for punch words. It sits centered in the middle third and builds 1-3 words at a time with a fade/pop. Sequence: 'You really / About to / Do it?' (~1.3-1.9s); 'Yes, we're coming to / Strongsville' (~2.0-4.8s); 'You really / About to / Do it?' (~6.0-7.5s); 'Cleveland's #1 Dessert Shop' (white, ~7.5-9.3s) plus 'Can't Fake / Influence' in magenta (~8.2-9.3s); 'Find / Your / Escape' (~14.3-17s, 'Escape' in magenta); 'They / Not / Like / Us' (~29.8-31.7s, 'Like Us' in magenta); 'When are we opening in / Strongsville?' (38.0-42.27s, kept on the white card); 'Very Soon.' in magenta (42.5-44.6s). No prices or item names.
study.audio: The only audio is the trending rap track 'Not Like Us' (all transcribed words are song lyrics, from 1.77s). There is no voiceover and no added ASMR, and there are no real pour or crunch sounds. Picture syncs to the song through lyric-matched text ('Can't Fake Influence' on 'fake influence'; 'They Not Like Us' on the chorus at 29.7s) and through cuts on beat hits (22.07, 28.5, 42.27s). Dense beat hits at 16.6-22.7s and 28.5-37.9s carry the fastest topping montages.
study.transitions: Mostly hard cuts. Focus-pull reveals from full blur act as soft transitions at 4.8s (Oreo sundae) and 31.7s (strawberry cup). A split-screen build: single frame to a 3-panel triptych around 1s, and a triptych again at 5.97s. A fade to white at ~40.4-41s into a white text card. A hard cut on an audio hit at 42.27s to the storefront.
study.effects: A 3-panel vertical split screen at 0-4.8s and 5.97-9.53s. Rack focus and defocus blur at 4.8s, 17.4s, 31.7s and 35.5s. Rainbow prism lens-flare overlays at ~9.7s, ~19.9s and ~33.9s. Slow push-ins and slides on hero shots. A bright, clean, punchy grade: lifted whites, saturated reds, pinks and rainbow cereal, glossy chocolate contrast, light sharpening. A white flash/fade card at 40.4-42.27s. No shakes or freeze frames.
study.quality: 720x1280 at 30fps, about 5.9 Mbps H.264. That is modest resolution, but the source footage is clearly shot on a proper camera with a fast lens: creamy bokeh, crisp focus on textures, smooth stabilized moves, clean exposure with no blown whites on cream, and low noise. Matching black gloves, branded cups, consistent backdrops and controlled lighting make it read as high-end, agency-made content rather than phone footage.
study.ending: It ends on the CTA, not on food. The text question 'When are we opening in Strongsville?' moves from the food (38-40.4s) onto a white card (to 42.27s). A hard cut on a beat hit goes to the exterior sign, then the new interior with 'Very Soon.' (2.33s). It cuts mid-pan with no loop intended, which leaves anticipation.
study.why_viral: 1) A trending, culturally loaded song, with text that puns on its lyrics ('Can't Fake Influence', 'They Not Like Us'), turns a menu reel into a meme-adjacent flex. 2) Extremely high-contrast, colorful, glossy desserts filmed as macro drizzles and pours: zebra chocolate, rainbow cereal, tiger-stripe boba. 3) A hyperlocal news hook ('coming to Strongsville', 'Cleveland's #1') makes locals share and tag. 4) Split-screen triptychs and about 1.9s cuts pack the whole menu into 45s, so it feels abundant and rewatchable.
lessons: Open on the most graphic pattern or motion you have (a feather drag, a drizzle stream) in macro, and put it on screen within 0.5s. Stacking 3 related macros in a split screen can triple visual density in the hook.
Keep shots between 1.0 and 2.5s (median around 1.9s, about 5 cuts per 10s) for a music-driven menu reel. Give finished hero items the top of that range (2-2.4s) with near-zero camera motion.
Build each money shot in three steps: 2-3 short 'making' shots (pour, drizzle, scoop at about 1.2s each), then a still 2s reveal of the finished item with the tagline on it.
Sync text to lyrics, not just beats. Reveal 1-3 words at a time when the matching word is sung, and use 2 text colors: a small neutral lead-in plus a large brand-color punch word.
Cut on the strongest audio hits for transitions that matter (new item reveal, final location shot). Check that the hit times line up within 0.1s.
Use a blur-to-focus rack pull of about 1s as a soft transition into a branded hero product, so the logo sticker becomes the focus target.
Shoot topping falls and drizzles at 50-60fps and play them back at about half speed so streams look smooth and glossy. Use black gloves to make cream and colors pop and keep hands looking clean.
End with a direct local CTA on a clean full-screen card (about 2s, text only), then a real-world proof shot (storefront or interior) with a short payoff line like 'Very Soon.'

study.format: Making-of / process video: a restaurant menu-launch 'build' reel, from raw beef ball to a sauced bowl, cut to a trending music track.
study.item: A 'Smashburger Bowl' from a Cleveland caterer. A griddle-smashed beef patty with a dark, glossy crust is topped with a melted white cheese slice. It sits on rice, chopped romaine, red pico de gallo (tomato, red onion, cilantro) and pickle chips, finished with a pink burger-sauce drizzle and a white sauce. Visual draws: deep brown sear against bright white cheese, vivid red and green veg, and glossy sauce ribbons cascading down the patty.
study.hook: First frame (0–0.67s): a macro eye-level shot of a raw, marbled pink beef ball on a dark griddle, with the bold centered title 'INTRODUCING CLEVELAND'S FIRST / SMASHBURGER BOWL'. The music opens and the vocal 'Who's cutting it?' lands at 0.78s. At 0.67s a spatula slams down on the ball in what looks like slow motion, with smoke and blur. The scroll-stopper is a local 'first' claim plus the anticipation of a smash on a raw ingredient.

Second angle of the press, steam rising, spatula edge filling frame.
